Friend, whistleblowers inside ICE have revealed something that should alarm every American.
**Under a secret internal policy, federal immigration agents are being instructed outright to ignore the Fourth Amendment: The bedrock protection that prevents the government from entering your home without a judge's authority.**
This policy violates public safety. It tramples on constitutional limits.
And, agents are being trained on this policy verbally, specifically to avoid creating a paper trail and to evade oversight.
Let that sink in: No written guidance. No public rules. No lawful warrants. Just verbal instructions to break into a home first and ask questions later.
Imagine a raid on your home, friend – not because a judge signed a warrant, not because a court found probable cause, but because an internal ICE policy told agents they could enter at will – for any reason. And, without risk of any consequence.
People should be afraid. Very afraid. It could happen anywhere. It could happen to anyone. _It could happen to you._
**And let me be very clear: This policy didn't appear out of nowhere. It comes from the highest levels of the Department of Homeland Security, under Secretary Kristi Noem's leadership.**
The head of our nation's homeland security apparatus has failed to stop federal agents from creating chaos, violating constitutional protections, and entering American homes without judicial oversight.
That failure is not accidental – it's by design. It's systemic. And it's unacceptable.
In a democracy, government agents do not get to kick down doors on a whim. They do not get to terrorize families in their own homes. And they do not get to ignore the Constitution because a political appointee told them to.
Secretary Noem must be held accountable. And she must be removed.
**I am demanding immediate answers, public hearings, and full accountability on this secret policy. But I need you standing with me.**
**_[The Fourth Amendment is not optional. It is the bedrock of our nation. Triple M tactics are simple:
* **Mask your identity**
* **Move as a coordinated mob**
* **Menace and intimidate your target**

Across college campuses, and in our streets throughout the nation and the world, these masked protesters dressed in coordinated black clothing and keffiyehs conceal their identities while harassing and, in some cases, physically intimidating Jewish students and supporters of Israel. They also preventing those from entering synagogues to worship; this is a clear violation of the religious freedom guaranteed in our constitution.

CAIR has challenged the order in federal court, and the legal dispute is ongoing. AG Pam Bondi dodged apologizing to the Epstein Survivors standing right behind her, bringing burn book documents spying on members of Congress.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260212-5911-footer&t=1&akid=5911%2E420207%2EztreKb)
Peter,
As I walked out after questioning Attorney General Pam Bondi, I knew this was a moment of truth. The truth was standing right behind Bondi—the courageous survivors of Epstein. The world saw her choose deflection over dignity, refusal over responsibility.
Pam Bondi refused a simple apology. She dodged my question. She couldn't even meet the survivors’ gaze.
**And now? The Department of Justice is spying on Congress as we search the Epstein files to hold them accountable.**
[](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260212.Coxqkk&refcode=em20260212-5911&t=2&akid=5911%2E420207%2EztreKb)
This is _outrageous_. Members of Congress should be able to conduct oversight without the Department of Justice spying on us.
Spying on my search history with a “burn book” of exactly what emails I searched is totally inappropriate. As a member of Congress it’s imperative I look for technical answers as to why exactly the DOJ thought it was okay to release the names of survivors while failing to investigate the predators that need to be brought to justice.
It is my job to hold them accountable, and it violates long established democratic norms for the DOJ to surveil us as we conduct oversight.
The casual disregard shown to the survivors, their trauma, and their presence in that room was unforgivable. Then to see a burn book spying on my search history of the “un-redacted” Epstein files took this beyond the law.
**We can’t undo the failure of Pam Bondi’s Department of Justice to keep survivors safe and bring predators to justice. But we can decide what happens next.**

Together, we can hold our government accountable.
In solidarity,
Pramila Jayapal

# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21486?t=1&akid=40832%2E3422442%2EZnRHDD)
Peter,
Do you remember 2006?

Dear Fellow American, A fifth-grade girl traveled with her Colorado school on a field trip across the country.

You can probably imagine how she must have felt in the days and weeks leading up to the trip. Excited to spend a few days with her friends. Eager to visit a new place. And, sure, a bit nervous--it's a big deal to stay overnight in a place you've never been before, especially as an 11-year-old.

**Now imagine how she felt when she found out --already hundreds of miles from home and in her hotel room for the night--_that she was supposed to share a bed with a boy._**

Shocked. Confused. Uncomfortable.

She slipped into the bathroom to call her mom, who was thankfully on the trip with her. Her mom thought she must have misunderstood. She couldn't fathom that the school assigned her daughter to room overnight with a boy.

But it wasn't a misunderstanding. It was _ school policy_.

The policy says that students on overnight trips will be assigned rooms based on their "gender identity," not on biology. And the school refuses to notify parents or students of the policy, or if a student of the opposite sex is assigned to the room.

That means a girl can be assigned to share a hotel room with a boy who identifies as a girl, without mom and dad's--or the student's--knowledge or say.

**How would you feel if this happened to your child or grandchild?**

It shouldn't have to be said--but this is just **WRONG.**

It's common sense that girls and boys deserve to have their own private spaces. And if that privacy could be infringed upon, parents need to know so that they can make informed decisions for their children.

Families across the country are being harmed by policies like these. That's why the Waileses, along with three other Colorado families, are pushing back in a lawsuit--for their kids and many others like them.

**Please raise your voice to say NO MORE to policies that deny truth and violate parents ' rights--and to protect kids from harmful policies that put gender ideology above their comfort and privacy.** [ SIGN THE STATEMENT](http://links.redconservatives.com/s/c/zCLePV4AKAwkR5Q3gD8GRI_bx67QGtvZKGfGR36PFfM_TQDGITBBcItCi59oapimW-kKrWRfjuxtgM-umsnylunBQDh1uC0BJl9y1PiiDsakny5GRXGqmKMKOr_uAKAx5G7uoonnhV_NLXmd3JgoGXVT8zotz0OUVDVPy5kUrZk0tb8p4Ydcelz7V8fuaBSTcLQT97TbOEB2OwJvTfMfl_nUXS6iN1VaCU0jwGnSrQ8b0mjeEuGVMnRdwEG6bS32cewab04VfrwQh5swlRtMxpTe175VCrE2HRdhvyL5MTE805NR1ILGayEcCAUTT5qmBYfiEuaO2eVEx9AxCHYSTpmhwAb3JztzjWl6n172vfkXX-aCkFYkYGDXbGM-S6ptAswp8Tf_n0v_1-jyOGelctl-tOKLkJkLlLLBsfTSe7jtE0Q3CF4gpvJV6wtml1CtjMjauw_NttEXzlw0zyPpJUtl8s3HWaLWjirUe5HWhUKKg_1lK3a5K1KDlQdF0wv9Ch5AiMpU_9SO1BYekWDQ2Y8MnkUrVWEmqoCwvqiD9quhYSPkXzcenGlrI3_EETcosYA2bvXiY_2UGu9JKuDc7wRKg1_6ZuYYszYvoREOZzS3FnpnYZcQ_4pBNSs3aXlYLaASpaZVWLljQcB0FbRwMIIONFwgT80fVGpEe9irCLpym7T36tHqFjQe2L_bHUzTcUBighsDz_Px0fHeMKxbSWz_eaWd/uN5pgBcBDjfg_nlz3MI21bQCir2atfJ5/17)

And the school refuses to notify parents or students of the policy, or if a student of the opposite sex is assigned to the room. That means a girl can be assigned to share a hotel room with a boy who identifies as a girl, without mom and dad's--or the student's--knowledge or say. How would you feel if this happened to your child or grandchild? It shouldn't have to be said--but this is just WRONG. It's common sense that girls and boys deserve to have their own private spaces. And if that privacy could be infringed upon, parents need to know so that they can make informed decisions for their children. Families across the country are being harmed by policies like these. That's why the Waileses, along with three other Colorado families, are pushing back in a lawsuit--for their kids and many others like them. Please raise your voice to say NO MORE to policies that deny truth and violate parents ' rights--and to protect kids from harmful policies that put gender ideology above their comfort and privacy. For truth, Sharon Supp Legal Counsel, Center for Parental Rights Alliance Defending Freedom P.S. Colorado parents are pushing back after the school district assigned their daughter to share a room with a boy. Alliance Defending Freedom 15100 N. 90th Street, Scottsdale, Arizona 85260

| | Fellow Patriot,
---
| | Charlie Kirk lived fast. And he lived loud.

He filled arenas. He lit a fire in the next generation on campus.

He confronted lies and spoke truth with boldness.

And he built a movement and a machine that few ever thought possible.

I saw it up close -- _Charlie moved at a pace most couldn 't keep up with. _

But in the middle of all the noise... he made a quiet decision that changed everything.

_**He started observing the Sabbath. **_

Not as a box to check. Not as a religious performance.

_But as an act of obedience. _

As a way of saying, **_" God, You are enough. And because You are enough, I need not carry the weight of a world that was never mine to hold." _**

Every week -- no matter what -- Charlie stopped.

He turned off the noise. He stepped away from the battlefield.

No email. No media. No work.

He gave his full attention fully to God, his wife Erika, and his children.

It was hard at first -- for someone who carried so much.

But over time, it changed him.

And before he was assassinated, he wrote a book about what he had learned...

clean_body: How Sabbath rest anchored Charlie’s life| | | | | Fellow Patriot, | | Charlie Kirk lived fast. And he lived loud. He filled arenas. He lit a fire in the next generation on campus. He confronted lies and spoke truth with boldness. And he built a movement and a machine that few ever thought possible. I saw it up close -- Charlie moved at a pace most couldn 't keep up with. But in the middle of all the noise... he made a quiet decision that changed everything. He started observing the Sabbath. Not as a box to check. Not as a religious performance. But as an act of obedience. As a way of saying, " God, You are enough. And because You are enough, I need not carry the weight of a world that was never mine to hold." Every week -- no matter what -- Charlie stopped. He turned off the noise. He stepped away from the battlefield. No email. No media. No work. He gave his full attention fully to God, his wife Erika, and his children. It was hard at first -- for someone who carried so much. But over time, it changed him. And before he was assassinated, he wrote a book about what he had learned... This was Charlie's final message. His final act of trust. A book not about politics... but about peace. It 's called: Stop, in the Name of God. Fellow Patriot, like I mentioned, this isn't a political book. It's not a culture war manifesto. It's a call to stop. To rest. To breathe. To return to God. Because Charlie believed America hadn 't just forgotten truth... It had forgotten trust. Trust that the world keeps spinning when you step away. Trust that God is in control. Trust that rest is not weakness -- it's worship. In Stop, in the Name of God, you'll discover: 🔥 How Charlie reclaimed the Sabbath in a world built on burnout 🔥 What sacred rest gave back to him -- as a father, husband, and believer 🔥 Why he believed this message could spark revival in a restless generation Charlie wrote this book because he knew what it meant to nearly lose his peace -- and what it felt like to find it again. That's the heartbeat of his final message. Charlie Kirk didn't waste his time on earth. He left behind a family. He left behind a movement. And he left behind this truth... For anyone ready to step off the treadmill... and walk back toward what's eternal. **PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**
| | Hi friends,
In 24 hours, the lights come on in Durango.
The podiums are set. The room is ready. **And Colorado voters are about to hear answers — not slogans.**
We’re one day away from the **[Colorado Republican Candidate Forum](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** , and the submissions haven’t slowed down. Voters are pressing candidates on TABOR, illegal immigration, election safeguards, school choice, AI regulation and the constitutional limits of state power.
As the forum approaches, **another candidate has stepped forward and asked to join the stage.**
**This isn’t a scripted rally. It’s a live test — and there’s still time to put your question in front of them.**
👉 **Submit your question[here](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**
Here is a summary of today's top stories:

🏔️ **Here in Colorado...** Rep. Jeff Crank and others warned [Colorado’s climate policies](https://link.email.joinrmv.) are driving up housing and utility costs, while a Denver7 investigation exposed [“ghost students”](https://link.email.joinrmv.) stealing millions in financial aid through identity fraud. Secretary of State Jena Griswold announced contingency plans for [“possible federal election disruptions,”](https://link.email.joinrmv.) and the Trump administration signaled it may withhold certain grants from Colorado and other Democrat-led states [over fraud concerns](https://link.email.joinrmv.).

🇺🇸**On the National Stage...** The House narrowly passed [the SAVE America Act](https://link.email.joinrmv.), sending the citizenship proof and voter ID bill to the Senate and setting up a showdown over election integrity. As Rep. Jeff Crank put it, “American elections are reserved for American citizens only,” arguing the bill simply requires documentary proof of citizenship and photo ID for federal voting. Meanwhile, [a grand jury declined to indict](https://link.email.joinrmv.) Democrat lawmakers tied []()to disputed military orders, and the DOJ unredacted additional names [in the Epstein files](https://link.email.joinrmv.) after bipartisan pressure—renewing transparency debates.

**🗣️ Commentary Spotlight...** Rep. Ken DeGraaf criticized [Colorado’s taxpayer-funded immigration policies](https://link.email.joinrmv.), saying they burden working families while incentivizing dependency and undermining the rule of law. Another piece cautions that ECMC’s updated [“high-priority habitat maps"](https://link.email.joinrmv.) could add yet another layer of regulation to Colorado’s already heavily regulated oil and gas industry. Dr. Joondeph argues the medical establishment faces a reckoning for putting [transgender ideology](https://link.email.joinrmv.) over children’s well-being, while a historical reflection warns that slogans like “stolen land” erode the rule of law [when grievance replaces principle](https://link.email.joinrmv.).
This is your Mountain Minute for Thursday, February 12, 2026.
– Team RMV

As a former CIA officer, I've seen democracies flicker out.

| Friends -

In November, myself and five other Members of Congress made a video quoting current law, that the military has a responsibility to refuse illegal orders.

In response, President Trump tweeted more than a dozen times, calling for me to be investigated, arrested, and hanged.

Since then, the FBI and former Fox News host Jeanine Pirro, now U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia, asked to interview me for the inquiry.

I wanted to share an important update on all of this, and ask for your help.

I wrote to Attorney General Pam Bondi and U.S. Attorney Pirro to inform them that I won’t be doing an interview -- and that their offices should preserve their records should I decide to sue for their infringement on my Constitutional rights.

I am not going to legitimize what they’re doing. The video in question was public, and I’ve talked about it extensively in the open. Our Constitution is crystal clear about our freedom of speech – and that’s a value worth fighting for.

To be honest, very smart people have told me to keep my head down and be quiet – that doing so would make this inquiry go away. But that’s exactly what Trump and Pirro want. They are employing physical and legal intimidation to get me to shut up. And, much more importantly, to deter other people from criticizing them.

So I’m taking the opposite approach, and I am fighting back, because this is bigger than any one Senator or any one video. If they can do this to me, what can they do to a business leader or the head of a community foundation or a mom who goes viral on the internet for criticizing Donald Trump?

And what people like Jeanine Pirro need to understand is that while the President of the United States may have immunity according to the Supreme Court, those who do his bidding do not. And if they are going to salute and do what he wants as part of this weaponization, they are going to own those consequences.

We all own our choices. I own mine. And Pirro and Trump must own theirs.

This is where I need your help. As I've said before, fighting back against these abuses of power requires a political strategy and a legal strategy. We're opening up an entire new front on the legal strategy -- one that goes on offense. But taken together, it requires resources, and that is why I am asking:

[Members of Congress have already identified hundreds of credible reports of abuse in immigration detention.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/125262274/601222636/484358469?sourceid=1151156&utm_campaign=26emeus-0201aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=investigateicedetention&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwM2RjYWNkMS00ZjA4LWYxMTEtODMyZS0wMDIyNDgyYTk3MzMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=nrGT5bn3gXkinM23GpZ-oVQRlQdj7Q8cUBKgneLQK54=&emci=2f48e6c8-3908-f111-832e-0022482a9733&emdi=03dcacd1-4f08-f111-832e-0022482a9733&ceid=954237) According to one senator's findings, pregnant women are waiting weeks for sub-par care, are being forced to sleep on the floor due to overcrowding, and are being denied adequate food and water.

[Immigrants who are pregnant, postpartum, or nursing should not be detained.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/125262275/601222637/484358469?sourceid=1151156&utm_campaign=26emeus-0201aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=investigateicedetention&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwM2RjYWNkMS00ZjA4LWYxMTEtODMyZS0wMDIyNDgyYTk3MzMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=nrGT5bn3gXkinM23GpZ-oVQRlQdj7Q8cUBKgneLQK54=&emci=2f48e6c8-3908-f111-832e-0022482a9733&emdi=03dcacd1-4f08-f111-832e-0022482a9733&ceid=954237) Pregnancy does not pause because someone is detained—and detention should never make pregnancy more dangerous. How can an administration that claims to be _pro-mother_ and _pro-child_ , allow this to happen?

clean_body: Miscarriage reports raise urgent concerns for pregnant women in ICE custody. | | | Peter, we are deeply concerned by reports of pregnant women in Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detention being denied adequate food, water, living conditions, and timely medical care. And tragically, some women in detention have suffered miscarriages. | According to one senator's findings, pregnant women are waiting weeks for sub-par care, are being forced to sleep on the floor due to overcrowding, and are being denied adequate food and water. Pregnancy does not pause because someone is detained—and detention should never make pregnancy more dangerous. How can an administration that claims to be pro-mother and pro-child , allow this to happen? Thank you for fighting with us in defense of dignity, care, and human rights. | | | | | | High school dropout. Waffle House waitress. First woman to graduate from The Citadel. Single mom. Fighter.

Nancy Mace wasn’t born into power. She worked for every inch of ground she’s gained.

At 17, she dropped out of high school and took a job slinging hash browns at Waffle House to survive. No silver spoon. No Ivy League connections. Just grit, grace, and a whole lot of graveyard shifts.

By the grace of God, she turned that struggle into a story no politician can touch. She made history as the first woman to graduate from The Citadel, South Carolina’s legendary military college. She built her own business. She raised two kids on her own. And when the Left came for everything she believed in, she stood her ground. Now, she’s running for Governor of South Carolina.

Nancy Mace is a battle-tested conservative who’s walked through fire and come out swinging. In Congress, she’s been one of President Trump’s fiercest allies, fighting to secure our border, protect our daughters, and stop the Left’s sick agenda dead in its tracks.

She’s not here to make friends. She’s here to make history.

Nancy is fighting to:

* Eliminate South Carolina’s Income Tax—the highest in the Southeast

* Prosecute violent criminals and pedophiles with zero leniency

* Crack down on sanctuary sheriffs who let illegal aliens roam free

* Defund radical public universities that indoctrinate, not educate

* Reform education so students learn how to think—not what to think

* Work hand-in-hand with President Trump to put South Carolina FIRST

Through every hardship, Nancy never gave up. And now she’s ready to do what she’s always done: roll up her sleeves, take the heat, and lead from the front.

South Carolina is worth fighting for. And Nancy Mace is just getting started.

subject: I need your help – Signature Day of Action
disclaimer_text: Paid for and authorized by Bennett for Governor · P
body:
As you know, we must submit 5,000 valid signatures from Maine voters to get on the ballot. This is a critical step and we’re inviting you to be part of a Day of Action on Saturday, February 21 to help us get there.

| | |
---
---
---
Hi Peter -- Thank you for supporting our independent campaign for Governor. As you know, we must submit 5,000 valid signatures from Maine voters to get on the ballot. This is a critical step and **we’re inviting you to be part of a Day of Action on Saturday, February 21 to help us get there**.

Here’s the plan: We’re asking volunteers to **commit to a 2-hour window** on Saturday, February 21, pick a location, and gather as many signatures as possible.

We suggest one of these high-traffic, community-friendly spots:
* A local transfer station
* Your local post office (morning hours)
* A local café (morning hours)

You choose the place and time that works best for you – we’ll provide the petitions, instructions, and support you need to succeed. If you need help finding a great location, just let us know and we can help!

**Why this matters**
Because I’m running as an independent, the rules are tougher – we need twice as many signatures as party-backed candidates just to qualify. That’s the price of independence.

As an independent, I listen to – and answer only to – the people of Maine. Not dark-money special interests. Not party bosses in Washington. I’m proud to stand with Maine voters who believe our government should work for people, not insiders.

But independence only works if people step up.

Detailed instructions for collecting, notarizing, and returning petitions will be sent to you, and the campaign team is always available to answer questions or provide additional materials.

If you can join us for this Day of Action – or want to collect signatures on your own timeline – [please sign up here](https://www.supportrickbennett.com/r?u=CvtCdFrMypuU80x-chHwl_ibJYNzwAgDoysqxMPE8iZHcgRf5qjw2bxOQAUemZPdHVVPWRgypR87OTMhRfUz71qA2msqV20cvYjL_xVZi20FNwnLcPqoiJzW2uXU1ABMW9AZJkIFSJLNWmVza9xpzQ&e=939e09e235be96b0bea768d960703804&utm_source=bennettforgovernor&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=signature_day_of_action&n=1) or simply reply to this email. We’d love to know where you plan to gather signatures and how we can support you.

I am grateful for your time, care, and commitment! Rick Bennett

name: Christopher Ahuja for Congress
subject: CA-32 Deserves Leadership That Fights Back
body:
The status quo is driving Americans broke.

| | | | | [|
---](https://chrisahuja.us2.list-manage.com/track/click?u=67424df89870d1cac00e55f46&id=060e293ac0&e=53c7d12fc7)
| | | | | | Dear Peter,While Washington floods the news cycle with chaos and political distraction, families in CA-32 are being crushed by rising costs and economic instability. Too many Members of Congress pretend everything is fine instead of fighting for the people they represent.
Wages remain stagnant. Underemployment is rising. One medical emergency can wipe out a family’s savings overnight. Rent, groceries, childcare, and basic necessities are becoming luxuries for too many hardworking people trying to stay afloat.
Instead of confronting this reality, career politicians protect their access to power, corporate donors, and a broken system that rewards billionaires while working families fall further behind. They offer talking points instead of solutions, press releases instead of results, and excuses instead of leadership.
Corporate politicians like Brad Sherman defend a status quo that keeps costs high and opportunity out of reach for too many in our communities.
I’m running for Congress because our district deserves bold leadership that refuses to accept an economy rigged against working people.
I am standing up to the chaos of this moment because my opponent won’t.
I’m fighting to:
• Lower everyday costs on housing, healthcare, childcare, and the essentials families rely on• Stand up for working creatives, freelancers, gig workers, and entrepreneurs who power our local economy• Invest in infrastructure, innovation, climate action, and good-paying local jobs that strengthen our communities• Protect and expand Social Security and Medicare so seniors can retire with security and dignity• Crack down on corporate price gouging and anti-competitive practices that exploit working people• Restructure our immigration and border systems to operate humanely, with dignity, and in accordance with the U.S. Constitution and the law
Every dollar we raise goes straight to powering this movement. To refusing to stay silent while families fall behind and corporate interests dominate our politics.
[**Join us. Stand with leadership that refuses to accept a rigged system and fights tirelessly for an economy that puts families first.**](https://chrisahuja.us2.list-manage.com/track/click?u=67424df89870d1cac00e55f46&id=904ba6c9fe&e=53c7d12fc7)
We got you.

## _Opinion:_
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e5c9fcf4-3e13-4b70-8241-889040e35b7c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**By** _Charles Sauer_
* * *
### The Capitalist is a reader-supported publication
### Reject Corporate Left Wing Journalism
[Support What We Do](https://substack.com/redirect/48d1b8bb-612a-4c55-923b-db40c03317f3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
Healthcare is intensely personal, and when devastating news arrives in the exam room, lives and families are changed in an instant. Yet a system bogged down by regulation and bureaucracy too often compounds that pain, forcing patients to navigate the most frightening chapter of their lives alone. We must change that.
That's why President Trump's plan to fund patients - not the system - is revolutionary. Shifting power from government bureaucrats, insurance companies, and big hospital systems will allow Americans to make their own healthcare decisions. When patients control the resources, the healthcare system begins to work _for_ them rather than _around_ them.
Today, one of the clearest examples of why this approach matters is Alzheimer's disease.
In a powerful **[Wall Street Journal op-ed](https://substack.com/redirect/0f28792a-c7af-4526-a607-938d8e0ac7ac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) ,** Dr. Brent Beasley recounts how he was diagnosed with Alzheimer's at age 57 after losing his job due to unexplained cognitive struggles. Despite being a physician with significant medical knowledge and strong connections, securing a diagnosis took nearly a year - precious time when early intervention can make a life-changing difference.
But Dr. Beasley's story is not one of despair. It's one of hope.
Because his disease was detected early enough, his care team successfully intervened. Treatment helped him regain clarity, remain active in his church, and live a purposeful life. His experience is deeply encouraging. You can read his story **[here](https://substack.com/redirect/0f28792a-c7af-4526-a607-938d8e0ac7ac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).**
**An Alzheimer 's diagnosis no longer has to mean immediate decline.**
Science is opening doors that did not exist a decade ago. Yet Dr. Beasley's story demonstrates that America's healthcare system is largely designed to react to crises rather than prevent them. Patients are often diagnosed too late even though early interventions and lifestyle changes can have profound impacts.
Removing barriers to early testing, expanding access to innovative treatments, and supporting caregivers must become a national priority.
There is another reason policymakers should pay attention.
Analysts, including President Trump's former Domestic Policy Advisor Joe Grogan and Paragon Research Fellow Ryan Long, increasingly **[warn that Alzheimer's is not only a medical challenge but an economic one](https://substack.com/redirect/d24ce4ac-e22f-4bc6-9b3d-cc9702bd15b8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).** Without a serious strategy, the growing number of Alzheimer's cases could strain families, shrink the workforce, and place additional pressure on federal programs.
**China has a plan. Where 's America's Plan?**
China has launched a national Alzheimer's effort focused on awareness, screening, and early intervention. America needs a similar focus. The health and wellness of our citizens and the fiscal strength of our nation are at stake.
The encouraging news is that the path forward is becoming clearer. It must include:
* Detecting the disease earlier
* Empowering primary care doctors
* Supporting innovation
* Reducing bureaucratic obstacles
* Putting patients back at the center of care

With the right strategy, America can lead the world by extending not just lifespan, but healthspan, allowing millions to remain active contributors to their families, communities, and economies.
Dr. Beasley reminds us that behind every policy debate is a human story and hope is no longer theoretical. Now the question is whether we will learn from stories like his and act boldly to help families facing an Alzheimer's diagnosis.

When patients control resources, healthcare system work for them, rather than around them. Feb 12 | | | | | | | | | | | Opinion: | | ---|---|--- By Charles Sauer The Capitalist is a reader-supported publication Reject Corporate Left Wing Journalism Healthcare is intensely personal, and when devastating news arrives in the exam room, lives and families are changed in an instant. Yet a system bogged down by regulation and bureaucracy too often compounds that pain, forcing patients to navigate the most frightening chapter of their lives alone. We must change that. That's why President Trump's plan to fund patients - not the system - is revolutionary. Shifting power from government bureaucrats, insurance companies, and big hospital systems will allow Americans to make their own healthcare decisions. When patients control the resources, the healthcare system begins to work for them rather than around them. Today, one of the clearest examples of why this approach matters is Alzheimer's disease. In a powerful , Dr. Brent Beasley recounts how he was diagnosed with Alzheimer's at age 57 after losing his job due to unexplained cognitive struggles. Despite being a physician with significant medical knowledge and strong connections, securing a diagnosis took nearly a year - precious time when early intervention can make a life-changing difference. But Dr. Beasley's story is not one of despair. It's one of hope. Because his disease was detected early enough, his care team successfully intervened. Treatment helped him regain clarity, remain active in his church, and live a purposeful life. His experience is deeply encouraging. You can read his story . An Alzheimer 's diagnosis no longer has to mean immediate decline. Science is opening doors that did not exist a decade ago. Yet Dr. Beasley's story demonstrates that America's healthcare system is largely designed to react to crises rather than prevent them. Patients are often diagnosed too late even though early interventions and lifestyle changes can have profound impacts. Removing barriers to early testing, expanding access to innovative treatments, and supporting caregivers must become a national priority. There is another reason policymakers should pay attention. Analysts, including President Trump's former Domestic Policy Advisor Joe Grogan and Paragon Research Fellow Ryan Long, increasingly . Without a serious strategy, the growing number of Alzheimer's cases could strain families, shrink the workforce, and place additional pressure on federal programs. China has a plan. Where 's America's Plan? China has launched a national Alzheimer's effort focused on awareness, screening, and early intervention. America needs a similar focus. The health and wellness of our citizens and the fiscal strength of our nation are at stake. The encouraging news is that the path forward is becoming clearer. It must include: Detecting the disease earlier Empowering primary care doctors Supporting innovation Reducing bureaucratic obstacles Putting patients back at the center of care With the right strategy, America can lead the world by extending not just lifespan, but healthspan, allowing millions to remain active contributors to their families, communities, and economies. Dr. Beasley reminds us that behind every policy debate is a human story and hope is no longer theoretical. Now the question is whether we will learn from stories like his and act boldly to help families facing an Alzheimer's diagnosis. Back in November, several of my colleagues and I released a video reaffirming a basic constitutional truth: the oath to the Constitution comes above all. No service member is required to follow an illegal order. Full stop.
Trump’s response? He tried to bully and intimidate us into silence.
He went so far as to have his allies at the Justice Department push for criminal charges against members of Congress for saying things he didn’t like.
**Donald Trump and his administration tried to intimidate us. Indict us. **
_But a group of everyday Americans sitting on that grand jury looked at this case and shut it down._
That almost never happens. Prosecutors almost always get the indictments they ask for. The fact that American citizens rejected this tells you everything—they could see what this really was: an abuse of power meant to punish people for standing up for the Constitution.
**Friend, even in this moment of intimidation and chaos, ordinary Americans still recognize the difference between the rule of law and raw political revenge.**
I first swore an oath to the Constitution as a 17-year-old at the Naval Academy. I took that oath again when I was elected to represent Western Pennsylvania in Congress.
That oath is sacred. It’s lifelong. It doesn’t expire. And it doesn’t bend to threats or tantrums from a would-be strongman.
America isn’t about loyalty to one man, it’s about loyalty to the Constitution. Defending that is something I will never shy away from.

Proof Democrats can win anywhere:
Gov. Andy Beshear is officially the most popular Democratic governor in the country, again.

This didn't happen by accident, Peter.

Andy didn't win three statewide elections in Kentucky by chasing headlines or playing politics. **He won by doing the work, showing up for people, listening to them, and delivering real results for their families and communities.**

And Kentuckians see it. Even in a state where Donald Trump won by more than 30 points in 2024, **Andy's approval rating is stronger among Kentuckians than Trump's right now.**

This is a clear message from voters about what kind of leadership they want. While Trump's policies are failing working families, driving chaos, and profiting billionaires and millionaires, Andy is focused on what actually matters: creating jobs, expanding healthcare access, prioritizing disaster relief, funding our public schools, and creating dignity for everyday people.

_No drama.

No ego.

Just leadership and results._

That's why Andy's playbook matters so much right now. At In This Together PAC, we're helping Andy support and elect more leaders across the country who govern the same way he does — leaders who put people first, keep their promises, and prove that Democrats can win anywhere by delivering for their constituents. What
happened in Minnesota is indefensible.

People murdered. Families ripped apart. Children detained in cage-like
enclosures. Communities living in fear of masked agents with unchecked
power. Although forces are supposedly now withdrawing from Minnesota, they
have left detrimental damage statewide.

Let’s be clear: ICE is no longer functioning as a law enforcement agency.
Under Trump, it has morphed into a militarized force driven by quotas,
shielded by impunity, and showing open contempt for basic human rights.

In the climate of fear created immediately after 9/11, Congress created
the Department of Homeland Security — a massive bureaucracy designed to
prioritize force over rights. In theory, it was designed to improve
information-sharing and coordination. In reality, it created a militarized
behemoth waiting for an authoritarian to come along and abuse it. And in
the process, it became a place where immigrants are treated as threats,
not people.

Something fundamental has to change.

The reality is that immigration should never have been placed inside a
domestic security agency built around fear, surveillance, and
militarization. It belongs in the Department of Justice, where enforcement
is governed by judicial oversight and constitutional limits.

That means:

* Ending immigration enforcement inside DHS.
* Breaking up DHS so it can’t operate as a domestic policing force.
* Ending ICE as an agency and returning its original function back to
the DOJ.
* Restoring accountability, transparency, and human dignity to the
system.

We must end a structure that rewards abuse. ICE operates untethered from
the legal culture. That’s how we got here. And until we fix it, no amount
of surface-level reform will stop the harm.

And instead of putting money back into the hands of hard-working Americans, Republicans signed the Big, Ugly bill into law that hands massive tax breaks to the wealthy.

Conspiracy theorists like RFK, Jr. have upended U.S. immunization recommendations, putting children at risk. subject: Tell your lawmakers: Tax Billionaires. Fund Pennsylvania.

body:
| | | Peter, As the 2026 budget season begins, Pennsylvania faces a defining moment. **Devastating federal cuts tied to Trump’s so-called “Big Beautiful Bill” have blown a multi-billion-dollar hole in our state budget.** Without new revenue, programs families rely on — Medicaid, SNAP, public transit, and public schools — could face serious cuts. **Lawmakers need at least $2 billion to prevent cuts this year.** Next year, that shortfall grows to nearly $5 billion annually as federal cuts continue and new unfunded mandates take effect. Last week Governor Shapiro announced his budget and it includes meaningful steps forward. Closing corporate loopholes and raising the minimum wage are long overdue. And making corporations pay what they owe is common sense. **But the scale of this crisis demands more.** **[Send a letter to your PA legislator today and urge them to tax billionaires and big corporations so we can fully fund the programs our communities rely on.](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm39flXHMmeMQ4GTaibnjUGBRWeWnJXbIzDVva6xYM13L-TDvbjv-kzZtHgcO0OC-oMQNOnkPHsvWL_GJrhLbQ-0489H9h4JPq07rX8mP8JqYlmG89_kWzYm9DjqQxnVEM6andGRz0tQh_fCfJSXywnqOu4UkUyuMVaNXLLqzFOh2RzDL-jjn-t05mbfsY1T6i9CRQAu0HfMS2tas8LJza4ISIGJXbGMoCr6c7c1Z0h-531pzgNizib0i5izmdkc5bGcYevIkgXaDt0loaNPTOu0AUZo33u9twf5n_-bQUt28LVqb3hY3xwfse9Hnes8bliI/4o3/2EnQcj-ZS0SWk_gWAo5-0g/h0/h001.jLceoD20121DZ4cpdVrVV9T-mt8cQ9MHRIPTu6AnthE)** **[Send a letter »](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm39flXHMmeMQ4GTaibnjUGBRWeWnJXbIzDVva6xYM13L-TDvbjv-kzZtHgcO0OC-oMQNOnkPHsvWL_GJrhLbQ-0489H9h4JPq07rX8mP8JqYlr9lowwDigNQuDz4XdnGsfh7C1Seaomc6PQ3uZqvDhp3OtqhvKyIYzt7fQhGrXLZpD5Tt_cWAztlkvEYVq_SVS9wCMTDGWzPLpdh491KTDfOkyfkDvy_CBYiCz-ldgomOgkxoSwvI75_y49Mb_iESpgRwU2HUSdPSlwC04dUDDUboQRml3WvcSrFQ5XyopdN_DCsotd3kS3is2GcWgcbMRQ/4o3/2EnQcj-ZS0SWk_gWAo5-0g/h1/h001.Ybu8roM6Cs3-Z3rcekpoobNMY5WVQDulHHjuedKCpLQ)** Pennsylvania can raise nearly $7 billion this year alone by requiring the wealthiest billionaires and biggest corporations in the state to finally contribute their fair share:
* **Close corporate tax loopholes** (~$1.5B)
* **Make Big Tech pay for digital ads cluttering our screens** (~$500M)
* **Tax billionaires’ unearned income** (~$4.8B)

**That revenue would protect healthcare, food assistance, transit, and schools — _without_ raising costs on working people.** This budget season, lawmakers face a clear responsibility: ensure that working families aren’t forced to shoulder the burden of federal cuts while billionaires and corporations continue to benefit from a rigged tax system. clean_body: | | | Peter, As the 2026 budget season begins, Pennsylvania faces a defining moment. Devastating federal cuts tied to Trump’s so-called “Big Beautiful Bill” have blown a multi-billion-dollar hole in our state budget. Without new revenue, programs families rely on — Medicaid, SNAP, public transit, and public schools — could face serious cuts. Lawmakers need at least $2 billion to prevent cuts this year. Next year, that shortfall grows to nearly $5 billion annually as federal cuts continue and new unfunded mandates take effect. Last week Governor Shapiro announced his budget and it includes meaningful steps forward. Closing corporate loopholes and raising the minimum wage are long overdue. And making corporations pay what they owe is common sense. But the scale of this crisis demands more. Pennsylvania can raise nearly $7 billion this year alone by requiring the wealthiest billionaires and biggest corporations in the state to finally contribute their fair share: Close corporate tax loopholes (~$1.5B) Make Big Tech pay for digital ads cluttering our screens (~$500M) Tax billionaires’ unearned income (~$4.8B) That revenue would protect healthcare, food assistance, transit, and schools — without raising costs on working people. This budget season, lawmakers face a clear responsibility: ensure that working families aren’t forced to shoulder the burden of federal cuts while billionaires and corporations continue to benefit from a rigged tax system. Pennsylvania deserves a budget that reflects our values and invests in a the multiracial, working-class communities that power this state. Trump, Netanyahu: No Deal

President Trump and Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu ended a nearly [three-hour White House meeting](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyc0D2OwyAUBODTQOcIHsQ4BcU27rLtlhaBl_AkfiyDvcrtV84RthtpNF8xP_fl7ihReX27jNYftIQallj3hr7mTL0jNlxbRyoR3QICxkHAIGEpaZE8WB9GBRytNEbclNQAPFqthQL041MbiUHroCcw4Qr66idnRsPJnpIACSBBaXlRMD2Uc-EZjNS3BzIt9jW4ju3ia2m4Ha7TgVRKPVMtF18zTzb2vjamvhjMDOYeMVJKZ8dgXmsi_2YwU-m4lc_MJQbz1Sg1iWno257XoWB35e3iPtDmypARO5UXg5lvNqy_lBK10TAtXtnRx-b9H1cdFv4CAAD__zCQePQ) on Wednesday with no agreement on Iran strategy. Trump said on Truth Social that "nothing definitive" was reached, but [insisted negotiations continue](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckL1urDAUhJ8GOiP72MDdwsVtttu0KdFZ-4Ct9Q_CBpI8fcQ-QrrRSDOa-T4f0wN98Gn5wEjaHH6y2U4u74VMjtHXSlRoLZV8coQTcBgYByZgSmESrdXGDhJa0mIc-U0KBdA6LWZuAI1QAns7GiX7mRvsYe7tTSkaWq-vJg4CQIBUopPw7ykR7WxHoW5PahTfV4uVSmdyKrQdWP1BPqV8qZw6k2MbtKt1LY3838C9gft5nt2cvxKdVyxeTt6CbeBetz2uLFHF9I1uZ5GostP5Suz9ljm_OFYqvqiwiuFVmN8wsQV_kK0BU7tpu54-BF-GsVF8iejDe0T9A7dDw28AAAD__0JugG8) — warning that Iran's refusal to deal last time ended with Operation Midnight Hammer. Netanyahu stressed Israel's security demands, pushing for any deal to include limits on Tehran's ballistic missiles and [an end to proxy support](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckLHO4yAQhJ8Gd0SwJuF3QXGNu__aK62N2Rh0BiyzNpe3PzmP8Hcr7cw3o_nzPX1jXGNefmMiN59x8sVPoRyV5pJSZCaqtFWmmAPhBAoeUoHUMOV10p13s3_00JHT1qqh1wagC87b10CzN9be70YN-PJKDXg39y8P1vTPLrqLpEADaOiNvvXw9ewR_ctbbYYnCaOOzSNTvc0lV9pP5HhSzLlcV8m3uaRudYF5q6L_JWAUMLbWbg1riHnhkjmmjz0JGDO1KmC8UgWML3oKGLX-PBjzG8Mhj30hSf82zJ68jDtmybj-rbIFmYg45kXyfqRNVnxXyRQuScPMF7nbnd9aXNdYH1YYtSSM66ck_2DX08H_AAAA__-JmYmz). Iran ruled out expanding talks beyond its nuclear program. ★★★
January Jobs Crush Expectations

The U.S. economy added 130,000 jobs in January — nearly double what [economists had forecast](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckL2SrCAUhJ8GMy044DAGBDcxm5tuaPFzZmRKOJag7rz9lvsIm3XS3V99X4_pYeMS8-u_TWj8EadAYZppL-gppVgrYsG1VIx5RjsBh1vLoRUw5WUSTTA-3CQ0aITWfJBCATSz4VwBcq0H58K977UcpFJ9r23PvROub6K5ljgIAAFSiU7C3UlrwzNooQaHTPF9DbZi6Tzlgtthazww5kxXotx5Ss1i5lrXwuQ_BiOD8TzP7knfbi8xY7mqicGInjKlD4NxL-2bXGk3XGmr7dvm3W6f9mJpNhPWMy5LLDfNFH8lG5ffk_oHL4eBnwAAAP__kcByvQ) — while unemployment dipped to 4.3%. Private payrolls surged by 172,000, with health care adding 82,000 positions alone. Federal government employment dropped by 34,000 as Trump's [workforce downsizing](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckDHOnDAQhU9jOiM8wLIULtK4-9OmRIM9wKzARrYB7Z4-YoscIN1I8-l9T-_Pz_CDvLKff-NG2p48uOCGJRyJbNg2zpko0Z4ysV8IB6jgISuQCga_Dqpw2rpHDQVp1XVVX6sGoFg0WXi2bU-1nayaiKwaoaMWJovWtv2zYH0nVaAAFNSNKmt4jjWim1ynmn4k0VTH7jBTKm3wieKJmU9i78N9BV_asBWrXnLek6h_CTACzHVd5RiJ84gx34QAQzb4sL0FmFspwFQgwCglwPxD5Xgk9pSSdDxTyjIvJOdImGWkPfKt_Hy1Er37fnHDD_tZvtAfGN_yFcZ0wyFmAaaI2u0XryunRyeaat6Q12_l_B8rnxr-BgAA__9gyo_Q) continued. Annual benchmark revisions revealed that the Biden-era economy added just 181,000 jobs in 2025 — down from the originally reported 584,000. President Trump touted the numbers on [Truth Social](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckLGOszAQhJ_GdI7stYND4eJv6PK3V6KF3YSNwEaxIXdvf0oe4bqRRppP831dhyvKIun-H1eO0yEDZRrmvBee8rpKrcyFt1JZ0sw4gIFWG9AWhrQMtqE4Ueug4WhDMJ2zHqCZ481A69l6f0HumCiMXRjH82Qu4UbUYiPxvWTAAlhw3p4cXEaHSDcK1ncjK2_2jbByOU05FX4eWOVgSSm_U06nKa_NEudat6LcPwW9gr7OPMuyvDsF_bgXSVyKgv4cHDgbdM2bfs1SWX8-ahTioiuum6b8SvqBacfnj37ksWj-3niqH5qCvnlG2l6yLFLaoLy5rygfUlP_IO6I8BsAAP__PMB_dA), calling them "FAR GREATER THAN EXPECTED." ★★★
House Passes SAVE America Act

The House passed the SAVE America Act 218–213 on Wednesday, sending the [election integrity overhaul](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJycUDtygzAQPQ10YqSVDHahIg2d06ZkZGkxOyO0GiRDktNn8BHSvVe879d9ujuKlJ6fbkXrd5oCh2nhV0HP60q1IhbMpSKlBd0EEnohQSiYUpxUG6wPvYYWrRoGedPKALSLhQGxd1LN6B4GTa_RG2dmf_FX3Rt5acmeThIUgAJtVKfh-tDOhTkMytwe2Bj5ysFVLJ3nVHDbXaUdKSU-EafO89pGu9SaS6M_GhgbGI_j6Gb-TnicsrWBMXOkSr40MHKKP4ITivc8EXAVO1cMgpKY3c7bm26Cgsgb8yw8VfrFVBbK4lUERvRncmk3G_JBMVLph8bI5-oovvvUf1y4W_gLAAD__zyMhPo) to the Senate. The bill requires photo ID to vote and proof of citizenship to register, with only one Democrat, Rep. Henry Cuellar of Texas, voting yes. Over 80% of Americans support [voter ID requirements](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckLGS4yAQRL8GZbhg0Ao7ILiEbC-9UDXArEWVAJUGi9-_sj9hs066-9X7971-Y95zff7FQi5eeU0trVt7McVWSu6diOngTrluhCsoWKQCqWGt-6qn5GJaDEzktLXqYfQMMG3ugfZu7JcJIcASFhXsor6iRmNJ33GJU3bvJQUaQIOZ9c3APRjE9JOsnh-BxKxeR8JOfIutMp0X9nxRrrW9U6u32Mq0u633g4X5I8AL8GOM20Decn32Vnsun3oR4CsNFuDfrwL8DwUBXmsB_tkOlowXSSx05ogSY5cHMhPLjwi5ESaWvLWR2qgyUWnxxM6SqWInAX46XTpG3vfMixWzehbM-4ew_0Lq5eB_AAAA__-q6IhW) across party lines. Senate Majority Leader Thune acknowledged the bill faces a filibuster fight, saying there are "not even close" to enough votes to [change Senate rules](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyc0L2u4yAUBOCngY7IHByIC4pt3GXbLS0MJ-Eo_FgGO6-_8n2E24000jfS_HsuT0eJyvuvy2j9SUuoYYn1aOhrztQ7YsOtdaQS0S0wgBYDCAlLSYvkwfqgFXC00phhUnIE4NE-zKT1ZNSK8qUniT4Yt4KRD_lya7grTvaSBpAAEtQobwoeq3IuvIKR47QiG4djC65ju_laGu6n63QilVKvVMvN18yTjb1vjak_DGYGc48YKaWrYzDHmrHgtzGYGxbXkcF8N0pJfRf52D_12z4k-n7kTWBCf7FipZREcycK5zuDme82bF9KiZo2bBze2dHPAO-_-Ou08D8AAP__FJJ7KQ) to force passage.

Sen. Lisa Murkowski became the first Republican senator to oppose the SAVE America Act, warning it [federalizes elections](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyc0L2u4yAUBOCngY7IHByIC4pt3GXbLS0MJ-Eo_FgGO6-_8n2E24000jfS_HsuT0eJyvuvy2j9SUuoYYn1aOhrztQ7YsOtdaQS0S0wgBYDCAlLSYvkwfqgFXC00phhUnIE4NE-zKT1ZNSK8qUniT4Yt4KRD_lya7grTvaSBpAAEtQobwoeq3IuvIKR47QiG4djC65ju_laGu6n63QilVKvVMvN18yTjb1vjak_DGYGc48YKaWrYzDHmrHgtzGYGxbXkcF8N0pJfRf52D_12z4k-n7kTWBCf7FipZREcycK5zuDme82bF9KiZo2bBze2dHPAO-_-Ou08D8AAP__FJJ7KQ) — the same argument the GOP used against Democrats' voting bills in 2021.

House Democrat Rosa DeLauro introduced legislation to fund every DHS agency — TSA, FEMA, Coast Guard, Secret Service — except ICE and CBP. body:
This week, two major election bills are driving debate in Washington about how Americans register and vote in elections: the Make Elections Great Again Act, often called the MEGA Act, and the SAVE America Act

| | | [ ](www.forwardparty.com)
---
### Peter —
This week, two major election bills are driving debate in Washington about how Americans register and vote in elections: the Make Elections Great Again Act, often called the MEGA Act, and the SAVE America Act. Both proposals would significantly expand the federal role in elections and place new national requirements on voter identification and registration. According to recent coverage from [IVN](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=rDd8ldfLFk-s1hATdsbsrVrIKpRzrH8t7maw10B8vrj60VSXOoGZuOzEjdjlq1S_1V8H0CNJuKwc-upvmads4C2dU2TmNsKtdyBk_r3MJkjHOi4DWzYHrTurC2iJgVWI&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_89a&n=1), the MEGA Act would create nationwide voter ID standards, tighten voter registration verification, restrict certain mail ballot practices, and limit the use of ranked choice voting in federal races. Analysts at[ Cato Institute](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=h4LJuM2PqUr84SzsJIXYhgZV_fNVF5PHXxmc1TEQkLJEp2vGj7e8i3XOmrpcbgnbsmZTgdbjmEy8nf37v9qheMMEPnYWLLjwf9567BYJy2eOkuRWxEmf23FWgRBmKyMZ&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_89a&n=2) have also raised concerns that the bill would centralize more election authority in Washington and reduce state flexibility in how elections are run. Separately, [Axios](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=N1PrSvDELWl4WPHU02ffpAPQb1krOqiA_VOKExDLVjE3jZMoiHr5sia-gFHLMus24_-35MI6pXQGtbVnYctLucxumdMHnDD2LOUlfr3r6jU&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_89a&n=3) reports that the SAVE America Act would require documented proof of U.S. citizenship, such as a passport or birth certificate, to register for federal elections, adding another layer of verification tied directly to voting eligibility. Public opinion on voter ID is more nuanced than the political debate often suggests. Multiple national polls over the past several years have shown broad support for voter ID requirements in principle, including support from majorities of Democrats, Republicans, and independents. At the same time, polling and academic research also show that voters express concern when ID rules are too strict, costly, or difficult to meet - especially for seniors, students, rural voters, and low income Americans who may lack ready access to underlying documents. In other words, voters tend to support voter ID in concept, but also want it implemented in a way that is fair and accessible. The Forward Party believes election policy should focus on two goals at the same time: strong security and broad voter participation. Voter confidence matters. Voter access matters. Good reform should accomplish both, not force a choice between them. That means if voter ID is required, it should be easy to obtain, widely available, and backed by modern systems that ensure eligible voters are not turned away. **Reader Poll: Voter ID** Do you support a legal requirement to present a valid form of ID in order to vote? Click the image below to submit your response. [](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=cwWx1Z7WVkSX5pP8jL35EOPKVe9uTMbIB69ocOWZfjP-2zEHkBwhrWGzsN20soXkt1Abo5FQMK-AneNaDnAP6w&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_89a&n=4) We will share the results in our next newsletter and use your feedback to guide our advocacy and messaging. Thank you for being part of the movement to build a more open, fair, and trusted democracy. **Forward this to your friends, family, coworkers - helps us introduce them to Forward and what we are trying to build. We would also love it if you could invite them to one of our upcoming events listed below.**

The next episode of The Forward Party Podcast is now live! In Episode 3 of The Forward Party Podcast*, Gov. Christine Todd Whitman, Lt. Gov. Kerry Healey, and Lindsey Williams Drath take a wide-angle look at one of the most important shifts in American politics: the rise of independent voters and the growing demand for a new political approach. Joined by veteran political journalist Chris Cillizza and professor and historian Dr. Jeremi Suri, the conversation explores what this moment means for the future of democracy and whether a new party can move the country forward. With nearly half of Americans now identifying as independent, the hosts dig into what that really signals. Is it frustration with polarization? A rejection of party loyalty? Or a deeper desire for common-sense solutions that neither major party seems willing to prioritize? Chris Cillizza offers an unfiltered look at today’s political climate, arguing that while the appetite for change is real, building a successful third party requires more than a headline-grabbing announcement. It takes grassroots organizing, credible candidates, and proof that independent leaders can win and govern. Dr. Jeremi Suri, chair of Leadership in Global Affairs at the University of Texas at Austin, places this political moment in context. He draws parallels to the 1850s and the Progressive Era, times when economic upheaval and social change disrupted existing party systems and opened space for new movements. According to Dr. Suri, when major parties fail to address pressing concerns, voters eventually realign around leaders and ideas that better reflect their lived realities. Together, the guests explore how today’s transformations, from artificial intelligence and workforce disruption to health care affordability and political disengagement, are reshaping expectations of government. The conversation challenges the idea that Americans are divided on everything. In reality, there is broad agreement on many core issues, but the current system amplifies the smallest points of conflict. We hope you enjoy! clean_body: This week, two major election bills are driving debate in Washington about how Americans register and vote in elections: the Make Elections Great Again Act, often called the MEGA Act, and the SAVE America Act | | | www.forwardparty.com Peter — This week, two major election bills are driving debate in Washington about how Americans register and vote in elections: the Make Elections Great Again Act, often called the MEGA Act, and the SAVE America Act. Both proposals would significantly expand the federal role in elections and place new national requirements on voter identification and registration. According to recent coverage from , the MEGA Act would create nationwide voter ID standards, tighten voter registration verification, restrict certain mail ballot practices, and limit the use of ranked choice voting in federal races. Analysts at have also raised concerns that the bill would centralize more election authority in Washington and reduce state flexibility in how elections are run. Separately, reports that the SAVE America Act would require documented proof of U.S. citizenship, such as a passport or birth certificate, to register for federal elections, adding another layer of verification tied directly to voting eligibility. Public opinion on voter ID is more nuanced than the political debate often suggests. Multiple national polls over the past several years have shown broad support for voter ID requirements in principle, including support from majorities of Democrats, Republicans, and independents. At the same time, polling and academic research also show that voters express concern when ID rules are too strict, costly, or difficult to meet - especially for seniors, students, rural voters, and low income Americans who may lack ready access to underlying documents. In other words, voters tend to support voter ID in concept, but also want it implemented in a way that is fair and accessible. The Forward Party believes election policy should focus on two goals at the same time: strong security and broad voter participation. Voter confidence matters. Voter access matters. Good reform should accomplish both, not force a choice between them. That means if voter ID is required, it should be easy to obtain, widely available, and backed by modern systems that ensure eligible voters are not turned away. We will share the results in our next newsletter and use your feedback to guide our advocacy and messaging. Thank you for being part of the movement to build a more open, fair, and trusted democracy. Forward this to your friends, family, coworkers - helps us introduce them to Forward and what we are trying to build. We would also love it if you could invite them to one of our upcoming events listed below. The next episode of The Forward Party Podcast is now live! In Episode 3 of The Forward Party Podcast, Gov. Christine Todd Whitman, Lt. Gov. Kerry Healey, and Lindsey Williams Drath take a wide-angle look at one of the most important shifts in American politics: the rise of independent voters and the growing demand for a new political approach. Joined by veteran political journalist Chris Cillizza and professor and historian Dr. Jeremi Suri, the conversation explores what this moment means for the future of democracy and whether a new party can move the country forward. With nearly half of Americans now identifying as independent, the hosts dig into what that really signals. Is it frustration with polarization? A rejection of party loyalty? Or a deeper desire for common-sense solutions that neither major party seems willing to prioritize? Chris Cillizza offers an unfiltered look at today’s political climate, arguing that while the appetite for change is real, building a successful third party requires more than a headline-grabbing announcement. It takes grassroots organizing, credible candidates, and proof that independent leaders can win and govern. Dr. Jeremi Suri, chair of Leadership in Global Affairs at the University of Texas at Austin, places this political moment in context. He draws parallels to the 1850s and the Progressive Era, times when economic upheaval and social change disrupted existing party systems and opened space for new movements. According to Dr. Suri, when major parties fail to address pressing concerns, voters eventually realign around leaders and ideas that better reflect their lived realities. Together, the guests explore how today’s transformations, from artificial intelligence and workforce disruption to health care affordability and political disengagement, are reshaping expectations of government. The conversation challenges the idea that Americans are divided on everything. In reality, there is broad agreement on many core issues, but the current system amplifies the smallest points of conflict. We hope you enjoy! Don't forget to let us know what you think. _**by Lawrence Winnerman**_
A former FBI Special Agent posts a warning. Releasing the Epstein files, he says, would unleash "a Pandora's Box of national security threats and geopolitical ramifications unlike anything seen before in American history."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a92702dc-c67a-4b16-aa66-b09aae19286c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Pandora's Box.
The phrasing is deliberate. It's meant to sound grave. A callback to one of our most foundational myths--the danger so great, so chaotic that even contemplating it is neigh unto suicide. As though what sits inside those files is so destabilizing that opening them would endanger the republic itself.
But that framing assumes something that millions of Americans, including me, no longer believe: that the current order is worth protecting.
**Pandora 's Box?
Fuck it.
**_**Bring on the dancing horses.***_
Because let's be honest about what we are actually living inside: systematic rape. Pedophiles. Power. Abuse.
_This is already a circus_. A disgusting, haunted circus with more rings of hell than Dante's Inferno. A vulgar, seamy carnival of power, money, and impunity. It is grotesque and predatory and corrupt at a scale so vast that polite language feels obscene.
We are not talking about an accounting error, or a blowjob from an intern, or missing minutes on tape. Those kinds of scandals seem quaint and somehow archaic at this moment.
Who wouldn't trade a thousand Trumps for a stained blue dress right about now?
We are talking about a network orbiting a man who trafficked underage girls to powerful men. We are talking about proximity between billionaires, politicians, financiers, media moguls--people who shape policy and markets and wars--and a convicted sex offender who somehow moved through elite society like more than a favored guest--like a ringleader. Like the circus master.
And the real fear, buried inside that "Pandora's Box" warning, isn't that crimes occurred. _We already know that they did._
* * *
[ Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.iC5LTAzpvgNsjy87Fm5Abgs5fb4BxtJIIL4LH8pCxXU?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=187788961)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a92702dc-c67a-4b16-aa66-b09aae19286c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The fear from the elite is what happens if the full web of crimes becomes visible.
Especially because that full web of crimes reveals the Machiavellian spiders feeding on the rest of us at the center of our current downfall: The Epstein Class.
I didn't come up with the name Epstein Class, and it isn't a partisan label. But it describes a global network of interconnected massive wealth, and we are all living in the world they have created.
**The Epstein Class** is the interlocking ecosystem of billionaires, corporate titans, political leaders across parties, financial institutions, media power brokers, and institutional gatekeepers whose wealth and influence insulated them from scrutiny -- and whose reflex, when exposure looms, is to preserve the system rather than submit it to truth.
They are not united by ideology. They are united by insulation--and that insulation is power.
For decades, many of us believed in partisan comity and incremental reform. I did. I was raised liberal, but pragmatic. I believed capitalism could be ethical if regulated. I believed institutions, though flawed, ultimately corrected themselves. I believed the American Dream was dented, not broken.
But what we are confronting now is not a flaw. It is an operating system that has been hacked by megabankers and techbros to work against the rest of us. Talk about enshittification--this is us discovering that Frankenstein's monster is real and hell-bent on killing us all.
This is what happens when shareholder primacy becomes moral doctrine. When Milton Friedman's theory--that corporations exist to maximize profit above all else--mutates into a worldview that treats everything as extractable. Labor. Land. Public trust. Democracy itself.
* * *
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3722532&post_id=187788961&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTg3Nzg4OTYxLCJpYXQiOjE3NzA5MzY4NzQsImV4cCI6MTc3MzUyODg3NCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTM3MjI1MzIiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.mNYHweqFsyQSWOUGX0bmlS492Ek5-C0Hvif_kwcfGAY)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a92702dc-c67a-4b16-aa66-b09aae19286c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The Epstein Class doesn't just rape people. It doesn't just rape children. They rape the earth. They rape communities of their small farms and good-paying jobs. They rape families of their life savings through financial games that socialize risk and privatize gain. They rape public institutions of legitimacy.
Their pedophilia is not an aberration. It is a proof of concept. It proves their mindset: _we are above consequences_.
And when that mindset fuses with global capital, political access, and media influence, you don't just get a scandal.
You get an entire class of people.
**Pandora 's Box?!
**_**Bring on the dancing horses, wherever they may roam.**_
Because the world order as currently arranged has been rearranging us for decades.
Housing out of reach for tens of millions. Healthcare bankrupting families. Wages stagnant while executive compensation explodes. Entire regions hollowed out in the name of efficiency. Endless geopolitical brinkmanship justified as strategic necessity while ordinary people pay the cost.
Stability, we are told, must be preserved.
But preserved for whom?
"It's time to move on."
-- Donald Trump
That was said during one of the earlier waves of renewed attention around the files. A call for forward momentum. For national focus. Definitely not accountability on his part.
"Americans are over the Epstein case... we need to move on."
-- Rep. Carlos Gimenez
A fatigue argument. People are tired. Uh huh. I know what they're tired of, and it ain't discovering that all the whispered conspiracies seem to actually be real.
"We're moving on from that."
-- Karoline Leavitt
Administrative closure. A pivot to other priorities. An articulated wish, maybe.
But notice what none of those statements address: **legitimacy**.
When elite proximity to a child sex trafficker becomes a footnote instead of a rupture, legitimacy erodes.
When disclosure is framed as a national security threat rather than a moral necessity, legitimacy erodes.
When billionaires and politicians move seamlessly through scandals that would destroy ordinary people, legitimacy erodes.
The Epstein Class hopes this cycles out of public consciousness. That the news churn buries it. That we accept partial transparency, curated document releases, redactions so thick they function as theater.
They hope we will equate silence with stability.
* * *
[Leave a comment](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3722532&post_id=187788961&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&isFreemail=true&comments=true&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTg3Nzg4OTYxLCJpYXQiOjE3NzA5MzY4NzQsImV4cCI6MTc3MzUyODg3NCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTM3MjI1MzIiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.mNYHweqFsyQSWOUGX0bmlS492Ek5-C0Hvif_kwcfGAY&r=1hvr60&utm_campaign=email-half-magic-comments&action=post-comment)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a92702dc-c67a-4b16-aa66-b09aae19286c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
But something has shifted -- and it isn't fringe radicalism. This isn't left versus right anymore. **It 's human versus anti-human**.
Protecting billionaires over justice for women and children is **anti-human**.
Designing financial systems that reward extraction over flourishing is **anti-human**.
Allowing corporate power and political authority to merge into a self-protecting aristocracy is **anti-human**.
If the full exposure of the Epstein Class network destabilizes that arrangement, maybe destabilization is overdue. Maybe it's time to choose the humans, and humanity, over power and money and technology.
**Pandora 's Box?!**
_**Bring on the dancing horses wherever they may roam
Shiver and say the words of every lie you've heard**_
If the truth rearranges the world order, then perhaps the world order was arranged around corruption in the first place.
We do not need literal fire, of course, to burn down this current world order. But we do need legal reckoning at historic scale. We need prosecutions where crimes occurred. We need transparency that is not filtered through institutional self-preservation. We need structural reforms that sever the seamless pipeline between wealth and immunity.
History remembers the Robber Barons. It remembers Teapot Dome. It remembers Watergate. Those moments forced recalibration.
* * *
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.iC5LTAzpvgNsjy87Fm5Abgs5fb4BxtJIIL4LH8pCxXU?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=187788961)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a92702dc-c67a-4b16-aa66-b09aae19286c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The Epstein Class may be the reckoning of an era defined by unregulated corporatism and elite insulation.
The question is not whether disclosure will cause discomfort. It will. _IT MUST_.
The question is whether we are willing to accept that discomfort as the price of legitimacy restored.
Because the alternative--the real Pandora's Box--is a society where the public no longer believes the law applies equally. Where wealth is indistinguishable from absolution. Where crimes at the top are absorbed as background noise.
That is not stability, it is deep decay.
We are not afraid of the dancing horses. We are afraid of a system so corrupt that truth feels like catastrophe.
If opening the files fully exposes the unredacted architecture of the Epstein Class, **then let it be exposed**. Let reputations fall where they must. Let institutions that cannot survive sunlight be rebuilt or replaced.
The world has already been fucked by the powerful.
Now comes the part where they answer for it.
And if that means the spectacle becomes undeniable--if the carnival lights come fully on and the headless horses start dancing--so be it.
**At least then we will all finally be looking at the same thing.**
