If transparency destabilizes the system, the system deserves to fall. | | and | Feb 12 | | | ---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- | | ---|---|--- Blue Amp Media is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support our work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber. by Lawrence Winnerman A former FBI Special Agent posts a warning. Releasing the Epstein files, he says, would unleash "a Pandora's Box of national security threats and geopolitical ramifications unlike anything seen before in American history." | | ---|---|--- Pandora's Box. The phrasing is deliberate. It's meant to sound grave. A callback to one of our most foundational myths--the danger so great, so chaotic that even contemplating it is neigh unto suicide. As though what sits inside those files is so destabilizing that opening them would endanger the republic itself. But that framing assumes something that millions of Americans, including me, no longer believe: that the current order is worth protecting. Pandora 's Box? Fuck it. Bring on the dancing horses.* Because let's be honest about what we are actually living inside: systematic rape. Pedophiles. Power. Abuse. This is already a circus. A disgusting, haunted circus with more rings of hell than Dante's Inferno. A vulgar, seamy carnival of power, money, and impunity. It is grotesque and predatory and corrupt at a scale so vast that polite language feels obscene. We are not talking about an accounting error, or a blowjob from an intern, or missing minutes on tape. Those kinds of scandals seem quaint and somehow archaic at this moment. Who wouldn't trade a thousand Trumps for a stained blue dress right about now? We are talking about a network orbiting a man who trafficked underage girls to powerful men. We are talking about proximity between billionaires, politicians, financiers, media moguls--people who shape policy and markets and wars--and a convicted sex offender who somehow moved through elite society like more than a favored guest--like a ringleader. Like the circus master. And the real fear, buried inside that "Pandora's Box" warning, isn't that crimes occurred. We already know that they did. | | ---|---|--- The fear from the elite is what happens if the full web of crimes becomes visible. Especially because that full web of crimes reveals the Machiavellian spiders feeding on the rest of us at the center of our current downfall: The Epstein Class. I didn't come up with the name Epstein Class, and it isn't a partisan label. But it describes a global network of interconnected massive wealth, and we are all living in the world they have created. The Epstein Class is the interlocking ecosystem of billionaires, corporate titans, political leaders across parties, financial institutions, media power brokers, and institutional gatekeepers whose wealth and influence insulated them from scrutiny -- and whose reflex, when exposure looms, is to preserve the system rather than submit it to truth. They are not united by ideology. They are united by insulation--and that insulation is power. For decades, many of us believed in partisan comity and incremental reform. I did. I was raised liberal, but pragmatic. I believed capitalism could be ethical if regulated. I believed institutions, though flawed, ultimately corrected themselves. I believed the American Dream was dented, not broken. But what we are confronting now is not a flaw. It is an operating system that has been hacked by megabankers and techbros to work against the rest of us. Talk about enshittification--this is us discovering that Frankenstein's monster is real and hell-bent on killing us all. This is what happens when shareholder primacy becomes moral doctrine. When Milton Friedman's theory--that corporations exist to maximize profit above all else--mutates into a worldview that treats everything as extractable. Labor. Land. Public trust. Democracy itself. | | ---|---|--- The Epstein Class doesn't just rape people. It doesn't just rape children. They rape the earth. They rape communities of their small farms and good-paying jobs. They rape families of their life savings through financial games that socialize risk and privatize gain. They rape public institutions of legitimacy. Their pedophilia is not an aberration. It is a proof of concept. It proves their mindset: we are above consequences. And when that mindset fuses with global capital, political access, and media influence, you don't just get a scandal. You get an entire class of people. Pandora 's Box?! Bring on the dancing horses, wherever they may roam. Because the world order as currently arranged has been rearranging us for decades. Housing out of reach for tens of millions. Healthcare bankrupting families. Wages stagnant while executive compensation explodes. Entire regions hollowed out in the name of efficiency. Endless geopolitical brinkmanship justified as strategic necessity while ordinary people pay the cost. Stability, we are told, must be preserved. But preserved for whom? "It's time to move on." -- Donald Trump That was said during one of the earlier waves of renewed attention around the files. A call for forward momentum. For national focus. Definitely not accountability on his part. "Americans are over the Epstein case... we need to move on." -- Rep. Carlos Gimenez A fatigue argument. People are tired. Uh huh. I know what they're tired of, and it ain't discovering that all the whispered conspiracies seem to actually be real. "We're moving on from that." -- Karoline Leavitt Administrative closure. A pivot to other priorities. An articulated wish, maybe. But notice what none of those statements address: legitimacy. When elite proximity to a child sex trafficker becomes a footnote instead of a rupture, legitimacy erodes. When disclosure is framed as a national security threat rather than a moral necessity, legitimacy erodes. When billionaires and politicians move seamlessly through scandals that would destroy ordinary people, legitimacy erodes. The Epstein Class hopes this cycles out of public consciousness. That the news churn buries it. That we accept partial transparency, curated document releases, redactions so thick they function as theater. They hope we will equate silence with stability. | | ---|---|--- But something has shifted -- and it isn't fringe radicalism. This isn't left versus right anymore. It 's human versus anti-human. Protecting billionaires over justice for women and children is anti-human. Designing financial systems that reward extraction over flourishing is anti-human. Allowing corporate power and political authority to merge into a self-protecting aristocracy is anti-human. If the full exposure of the Epstein Class network destabilizes that arrangement, maybe destabilization is overdue. Maybe it's time to choose the humans, and humanity, over power and money and technology. Pandora 's Box?! Bring on the dancing horses wherever they may roam Shiver and say the words of every lie you've heard If the truth rearranges the world order, then perhaps the world order was arranged around corruption in the first place. We do not need literal fire, of course, to burn down this current world order. But we do need legal reckoning at historic scale. We need prosecutions where crimes occurred. We need transparency that is not filtered through institutional self-preservation. We need structural reforms that sever the seamless pipeline between wealth and immunity. History remembers the Robber Barons. It remembers Teapot Dome. It remembers Watergate. Those moments forced recalibration. | | ---|---|--- The Epstein Class may be the reckoning of an era defined by unregulated corporatism and elite insulation. The question is not whether disclosure will cause discomfort. It will. IT MUST. The question is whether we are willing to accept that discomfort as the price of legitimacy restored. Because the alternative--the real Pandora's Box--is a society where the public no longer believes the law applies equally. Where wealth is indistinguishable from absolution. Where crimes at the top are absorbed as background noise. That is not stability, it is deep decay. We are not afraid of the dancing horses. We are afraid of a system so corrupt that truth feels like catastrophe. If opening the files fully exposes the unredacted architecture of the Epstein Class, then let it be exposed. Let reputations fall where they must. Let institutions that cannot survive sunlight be rebuilt or replaced. The world has already been fucked by the powerful. Now comes the part where they answer for it. And if that means the spectacle becomes undeniable--if the carnival lights come fully on and the headless horses start dancing--so be it. At least then we will all finally be looking at the same thing. | | ---|---|--- READ MORE FROM BLUE AMP MEDIA | | and | | ---|---|--- | Feb 9 | | | and | | ---|---|--- | Feb 9 | | | and | | ---|---|--- | Feb 6 | * You're currently a free subscriber to . body:
Critics attacked me for speaking out in 2020 – now the evidence is catching up.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://us10.campaign-archive.com/?e=4d3fe76c62&u=c9a64ea8a402e6526a97d9207&id=5b419aa40e)

| | | | | | Peter,
As your candidate for Congress in Texas' 21st District, I want to share something personal and principled with you ahead of the March 3, 2026, Republican Primary.
In November 2020, as Chairman of the Federal Election Commission (appointed by President Trump), I spoke plainly about the evidence emerging from the presidential election. In a widely [**reported interview covered by The Epoch Times**](https://Trey4TX.us10.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c9a64ea8a402e6526a97d9207&id=c97bb46a76&e=4d3fe76c62) on November 17, 2020, I said that if Sidney Powell—then advancing claims backed by thousands of sworn affidavits—said there was rampant voter fraud, "**I believe her**." I stood by that because the volume of testimonies, irregularities, and procedural failures demanded scrutiny, not dismissal.
That statement drew fierce criticism. On X ([@TXElectionLaw](https://Trey4TX.us10.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c9a64ea8a402e6526a97d9207&id=520554485e&e=4d3fe76c62)), detractors called me a conspiracy theorist, demanded my resignation, and accused me of undermining democracy. Some Republicans distanced themselves to avoid backlash. The attacks were intense and unrelenting.
**But I never backed down**. Why? Because protecting election integrity is non-negotiable. I've fought for fair, transparent elections my entire career—through my work as General Counsel to the Texas Secretary of State and the Republican Party of Texas, and during my FEC tenure where I pushed for accountability and transparency.
Recent developments in Georgia vindicate that early stance. In late January 2026, the FBI executed a search warrant at Fulton County's election hub, seizing hundreds of boxes of 2020 ballots, voter rolls, ballot images, and related materials. This unprecedented action—driven by ongoing probes into alleged irregularities—includes reports of duplicate ballots, chain-of-custody failures, and unsecured processes in a county central to 2020 controversies. Fulton officials are challenging the seizure, but the fact remains: questions from 2020 persist, and federal authorities are finally acting on them.
I've endured criticism, two Inspector General investigations (one over a mislabeled event in Denton County, another for refusing the Biden vaccine mandate), and financial sacrifices from my FEC role—all while staying true to principle. My family and I have paid a price, but we did it because our country and our elections are worth it.
**This is who I am: a fighter who believes in the evidence, stands firm under fire, and won't compromise on election security.** In Congress, I'll sponsor legislation for nationwide voter ID, bans on ballot harvesting, mandatory audits, and hand-counted paper ballots in high-risk jurisdictions. I'll push to codify reforms that prevent future interference and restore trust.
TX-21 deserves a representative who won't fold when the stakes are high. I've proven I won't. Now, I humbly ask for your vote in the March primary. Early voting begins February 17, 2026—let's secure our elections and our future together.
Please visit [**trey4tx.com**](https://Trey4TX.us10.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c9a64ea8a402e6526a97d9207&id=96fcfed0e8&e=4d3fe76c62) to learn more, [**volunteer**](https://Trey4TX.us10.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c9a64ea8a402e6526a97d9207&id=e69ca25317&e=4d3fe76c62) , or[**contribute**](https://Trey4TX.us10.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c9a64ea8a402e6526a97d9207&id=a20352d633&e=4d3fe76c62). Together, we'll win this seat and make a real difference.
For integrity, for Texas, for America First,
**Trey Trainor** Husband, Father of 6,Proven Conservative Fighter for TX-21

Peter, big news out of D.C. last night: House Republicans passed an extreme, anti-voter bill they’re calling the “SAVE America Act” — let’s be clear: **This legislation would make it nearly impossible for millions of eligible American citizens to register to vote.** Here’s the good news: We defeated similar legislation in the Senate last year thanks to pushback from the American people. But because Republicans don’t have the votes, **some senators want to nuke the filibuster to pass this bill. ** That’s right. These guys are so desperate to shut out certain Americans from participating in our democracy, that they’re willing to change the Senate rules to pass it. As Sen. Ted Cruz put it, “That’s what I’m urging my colleagues to do. It’s what President Trump wants us to do. And it’s what I hope and pray we accomplish.” [**This is an urgent moment to stand up for our democracy. Will you rush a donation to support the NDRC and help defeat authoritarian power plays like the SAVE Act?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/125267458/601240735/-2069046819?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_SAVEActRR_email_20260212-NDRC-Tier1-SAVEActRR_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20260212-NDRC-Tier1-SAVEActRR_&utm_campaign=SAVEActRR&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImRiM2FkMTM4LTVlMDgtZjExMS04MzJlLTAwMjI0ODJhOTczMyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=cSytb34ukoIGblGIaWX7Kxqus1lhL8exCTYROhy_t2c=) Have you noticed a pattern? When public opinion turns against President Trump and the MAGA agenda, Republicans will try anything to tamp down the will of the people. That’s why they launched a national gerrymandering crisis last summer — passing mid-decade map redraws in states like Texas, Missouri, and North Carolina to try to avoid losing power in the midterm elections. And it’s why they now want to change the law to make it harder to vote. They call it “common-sense” to require Americans to prove their citizenship when registering to vote, saying it’s needed to combat voter fraud. What they don’t tell you is that this kind of fraud is so rare that someone is more likely to get struck by lightning than to try it. They want millions of Americans to show their papers — bringing birth certificates and marriage licences to the polls to solve a problem that simply doesn’t exist. (Heaven help you if you lost documents in a move or in a flood or a house fire.) These are unreasonable, unnecessary hurdles. Their desired effect is to disenfranchise people who can’t jump through them. That’s what they want: fewer Americans voting. clean_body: This bill would make it nearly impossible for millions of Americans to vote. | Peter, big news out of D.C. last night: House Republicans passed an extreme, anti-voter bill they’re calling the “SAVE America Act” — let’s be clear: This legislation would make it nearly impossible for millions of eligible American citizens to register to vote. Here’s the good news: We defeated similar legislation in the Senate last year thanks to pushback from the American people. But because Republicans don’t have the votes, some senators want to nuke the filibuster to pass this bill. That’s right. These guys are so desperate to shut out certain Americans from participating in our democracy, that they’re willing to change the Senate rules to pass it. As Sen. Ted Cruz put it, “That’s what I’m urging my colleagues to do. It’s what President Trump wants us to do. And it’s what I hope and pray we accomplish.” = Have you noticed a pattern? When public opinion turns against President Trump and the MAGA agenda, Republicans will try anything to tamp down the will of the people. That’s why they launched a national gerrymandering crisis last summer — passing mid-decade map redraws in states like Texas, Missouri, and North Carolina to try to avoid losing power in the midterm elections. And it’s why they now want to change the law to make it harder to vote. They call it “common-sense” to require Americans to prove their citizenship when registering to vote, saying it’s needed to combat voter fraud. What they don’t tell you is that this kind of fraud is so rare that someone is more likely to get struck by lightning than to try it. They want millions of Americans to show their papers — bringing birth certificates and marriage licences to the polls to solve a problem that simply doesn’t exist. (Heaven help you if you lost documents in a move or in a flood or a house fire.) These are unreasonable, unnecessary hurdles. Their desired effect is to disenfranchise people who can’t jump through them. That’s what they want: fewer Americans voting. A lot of folks are raising the alarm about interference in the midterm elections right now — and I agree that we should all be concerned.
Let’s start here: It’s obvious that Donald Trump would like to interfere in our elections.
He’s made that abundantly clear — from his recent comments about nationalizing the election to seizing 2020 ballots from the Fulton County election office.
Then we have people like Steve Bannon saying the administration should send ICE agents to polling places — and Karoline Leavitt publicly not ruling it out.
And frankly, we can’t trust Mike Johnson to stop this kind of anti-democratic interference, because he was the legal architect behind Trump’s effort to overturn the election results in 2020!
So that’s all pretty terrifying. But here’s the good news: Our election system is very resilient. The fact that election administration is distributed across each state and each county makes it much harder for Trump to be able to get in the way.
There are two main things I think we need right now to put an end to this:
First, we need more Republicans to stand up to Trump and reject these kinds of un-American threats. I’m glad some GOP Members of Congress have spoken out — but it’s not enough. They have the power to stop this, and they have to do more.
Second — and much more in our control than hoping congressional Republicans grow a spine — we need to win by such a huge margin that they can’t possibly overturn the results.
And I believe we can do it . What we’ve seen in every single special election since 2024 is that people very clearly understand what this administration is up to, and they want a check on Donald Trump’s power.
But it won’t happen on its own. We need to put in the work. That’s what my campaign team and I are focused on right now — building out our plans to win my election, support Democratic colleagues in tough races, and power Democratic challengers aiming to flip key seats.

Hi Peter,
The 2026 short session is underway, and we’re already seeing a dangerous Major Threat ( SB 1586 [https://olis.oregonlegislature.gov/liz/2026R1/Measures/Overview/SB1586] ) to long-standing agreements and Oregon’s land use laws.
SB 1586 would open up 1,700 acres of world-class farmland, by expanding the Metro urban growth boundary into land protected as rural reserves and zoned exclusively for farm use. This land was explicitly safeguarded through a 2014 legislative settlement that every stakeholder agreed to honor known as the grand bargain [https://www.oregonlive.com/politics/2014/03/land_use_grand_bargain_heading.html] . In this exchange, Hillsboro received over 1,000 acres of farmland for industrial use. This bill breaks that promise and opens the door to another speculative land grab. Once this farmland is gone, it’s gone forever. And it’s not needed: Oregon already has thousands of acres of industrial land inside cities, including in Hillsboro.
This bill has not been scheduled for a public hearing yet. Please send your message to your legislators today to stop this Major Threat! [https://secure.ngpvan.com/bZ-sIesX6E--D_ksOxy7VQ2]
Stop this Major Threat [https://secure.ngpvan.com/bZ-sIesX6E--D_ksOxy7VQ2?contactdata=zg2bt1x3MQ4f51AaC7HO0mSHw74OszfVXOr9Zb0sT+tQEr63g0D4KuC1ulg7zGsz1M7DknlUw/gqT0XH1k1Pk+miOdYhFmNVtKcLLWcnn9eUGkZllv/SGB7oFlbC4fx6]
Oregon’s land use system exists because people fought for it. If we don’t speak up now, we risk losing these lands piece by piece.
Together,
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/AV/AVLCV/1/70877/images/Eliza.png]
Eliza Walton (she/they)
OLCV Coalition Director

| Peter, Here’s why I voted **NO** on the SAVE Act.

Republicans claim this bill is about “election security.” It is not. It is about making voting harder. And here’s how: **❌** It would require Americans to show proof of citizenship at polling places, such as a passport or birth certificate — documents that millions of Americans do not carry with them.

**❌** It would force Americans to spend up to $130 to obtain paperwork just to exercise their constitutional right to vote.

**❌** It would disproportionately target women whose married names do not match their birth certificates, seniors, military families, rural voters, and newly naturalized citizens. In other words, it would disenfranchise millions.

**❌** And it would cost taxpayers an estimated $19 billion nationwide.

name: Sen. Jeff Bridges
subject: Taking on TABOR and endorsed by CEA
body:
I’m already leading the fight to raise our TABOR rationing cap. The Colorado Education Association and I have a measure to raise TABOR cap

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/9b9fb6df13e0/get-more-smarter-on-colorados-budget-10372657?e=b48bb2b4f4)
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/Z5hLUpw_xAN?e=b48bb2b4f4&c2id=bbe572662fdb5fed2d0855c1bcb00da8)
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Hi there,
As Democrats we talk a lot about TABOR. But addressing the fiscal crisis caused by Trump and TABOR needs more than just talk.
**I’m already leading the fight this year to raise our TABOR rationing cap.** The Colorado Education Association and I have developed a referred measure that would, [as the Colorado Sun put it](https://us.list-manage.com/hzQ1_KbOtMl?e=b48bb2b4f4&c2id=bbe572662fdb5fed2d0855c1bcb00da8), “ask voters to raise TABOR cap by billions primarily to fund Colorado’s schools.”
**It’s just one reason why the Colorado Education Association has endorsed my campaign for State Treasurer.**
This one means a lot to me.
I’ve spent the last decade in the Legislature fighting for teachers and students. I’ve chaired the Education Committee. I passed fully funded full-day kindergarten unanimously. I’ve balanced budgets that protected classrooms during tough years. And my mom, grandma, aunt, mother-in-law, and brilliant wife were all teachers—Thanksgiving would have been very awkward if I hadn’t earned this endorsement!
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/_6IobCaGbqq?e=b48bb2b4f4&c2id=bbe572662fdb5fed2d0855c1bcb00da8)
| |
Colorado ranks near the bottom nationally in what we invest in K–12 public education. That’s not because Colorado doesn’t value education. It’s because our constitution artificially restricts our ability to invest in it.
**The measure CEA and I are working on would raise the TABOR cap, Ref C–style, so we can finally fund our schools at the level our students and teachers deserve.** It would move Colorado from the bottom tier of education funding to one of the top states in the country, lower class sizes, increase pay, and improve workforce readiness. And we’d have an audit to make sure we deliver on these promises.
Nothing radical. Nothing reckless.
Just the simple idea that when our economy grows, our investment in education should grow with it.
I believe budgets are moral documents. They show, in dollars and cents, what we value. Right now, TABOR distorts those values. I hope you’ll support this measure on your ballot in November.
**And if you plan to attend State Assembly, please reply to this email and let me know! Or text my personal cell at 303-358-5551.**
More soon, including some work I’m doing to build housing for teachers across the state.
---
| | Talk soon,
P.S. The polling on this measure is actually really good, which matters because even the best ideas don’t make a difference if they don’t pass.

Friend,

**House Republicans just passed the SAVE America Act -- one of the most dangerous anti-voter, anti-democracy bills we’ve seen in years. I was proud to vote _NO_.**

While they claim this bill is about election security and stopping undocumented immigrants from voting, something that is _already_ illegal, in reality it will make it much harder for everyday Americans to vote.

There are over 70 MILLION Americans who have legal names that no longer match their birth certificate -- women who have changed their last names after marriage, for example. Under the SAVE America Act, they would be unable to vote without obtaining new certification. This legislation also threatens state systems like vote-by-mail and streamlined voter registration that has made life easier.

This would be especially tough on rural communities, in Illinois and beyond, where folks would be forced to take time off of work, travel for hours, and pay fees _just to exercise what should already be a fundamental right._

**Republicans want to take us backwards, not improve access to the ballot box. This is a clear sign of their real intentions -- to make it harder for Americans to be heard in the hopes of expanding their grip on power.**

Meanwhile, I’m making it my mission to protect our democracy -- and don’t just take my word for it. I’ve been endorsed by groups including the League of Conservation Voters, Defend the Vote, and more who understand the importance of this moment.

**[This fight doesn’t end here. The GOP knows this won’t stand if they lose their majority in November -- and it starts with races like this one. Friend, DHS and ICE have carried out a full-scale assault on our civil rights and our Constitution under the leadership of Trump and Kristi Noem.
Their strategy has been to exploit people who may not know the law, deceive people into forfeiting their rights, and abuse gray areas in what is and isn’t legal.
ICE may have announced a pullback in Minnesota, but their agents still roam the streets in our state and across the country. That’s why Team Ilhan is doing everything we can to make sure Minnesotans and all Americans know their rights when dealing with ICE.
Here’s five things we think EVERYONE should know:
* **ICE and Border Patrol cannot open your door and come into your house without a valid judicial warrant, signed by a judge with your correct name or address on it.**

* **If questioned or detained by immigration agents, you have the right to remain silent and the right to speak to an attorney.**

* **You do not have to sign anything or agree to anything without an attorney present.**

* **If you witness ICE activity such as a raid or arrest, you have the right to document it through videos, photos, and written documentation.**

* **Carry any valid immigration documents you may have, make an emergency plan with your family, contact a lawyer in advance, and memorize at least one emergency phone number.**

As ICE’s crackdowns continue, everyone should be ready to assert their rights. That’s why we’re hosting Know Your Rights trainings, sharing this information throughout our community, and directing our neighbors to legal resources.

name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: Did you know ICE agents get only 47 days of training? Want to guess why 47?
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:
| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=2771%2E4032634%2EpVl5E6)
---
Did you know ICE agents get only 47 days of training before they’re handed a gun and sent out into American streets? Why 47? In honor of Trump being the 47th President, of course. So the Trump administration is just picking these numbers in the name of vanity. Got it. As Trump treats this like a fun little game, Americans are being shot and killed in the streets. Children are being swiped up by their backpacks by agents. Families are afraid to leave their homes to simply go to school or the grocery store. If we’re going to pick out some numbers to focus on, in addition to the egregiously short period of time these recruits spend on training before they are sent to cities with loaded guns and are told they have full immunity, here’s a few more we should be considering: **$85 billion.** That’s how much funding ICE received from Trump in last year’s Big, Ugly Bill. This made ICE the country’s highest-funded law enforcement agency, all due to cuts to health care and food assistance funding. **$190 billion.** That’s how much overall funding was given towards Trump’s DHS and immigration crackdown. That is bigger than the annual military budget of every country in the world — combined — except for the United States and China. **$10 billion.** That’s how much extra money Republicans want to give ICE right now. Because being the highest-funded law enforcement agency and beating out all but two countries’ total military spending combined is not enough. **73,000.** That’s the record-high number of people detained by immigration enforcement as of January 2026. That’s an **84%** increase compared to this same time last year. **86% of those arrested** by ICE during Trump’s first year back in office had no violent criminal records. There has been a **2,450% increase** in the number of people with no criminal record being held in ICE detention on any given day. In 2025, **more than 170 U.S. Citizens** were held by immigration agents. Nearly 20 of them were children. 2 of those children had cancer. **At least 38 people** have died while in ICE custody since Trump took office. **4 people** were fatally shot by ICE agents. These aren’t just numbers. They’re painful stories. They’re human lives. They’re evidence of a system fueled by vanity, driven by cruelty, and engineered for unchecked power — all paid for with our tax dollars. This didn’t happen overnight — and it won’t be undone without sustained, people-powered pressure. The most immediate thing we can do right now is block more DHS funding and use our leverage to rein in the terror and violence coming from ICE right now. That’s just the start — and I’m in this fight all the way. Elizabeth

name: Lizzie Fletcher
subject: At a time when nothing feels like it is enough – doing something is important
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY ELIZABETH PANNILL FLETCHER FOR CONGRESS
body:
ELIZABETH PANNILL FLETCHER FOR CONGRESS [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP10/1/82676/images/Non-Re-Elect%20Logo.png]
Lately, I have been thinking about all that is happening around us—how to make sense of it, how to respond to it, how to change it. I have heard from so many people that they feel overwhelmed by the enormity of the challenges we face. Nothing they can do feels like enough. (And, they tell me nothing Congress is doing feels like enough, either.)
I know how this feels. This is my every day. But I also know that everything we do is something. And all those things we do add up to something meaningful. Something that matters. And these days, there are a lot of somethings we can do (even if it doesn’t feel like it).
Of course, primary elections are almost underway in Texas. Early voting starts next week. We can vote and mobilize voters from now to next November. In fact, we must mobilize voters from now until then to make sure we take back the House of Representatives to put a check on this lawless administration.
Those who saw yesterday’s hearing before the House Judiciary Committee, or parts of it, were reminded of how lawless it is, and how far we have fallen. The Attorney General of the United States, Pam Bondi—the top law enforcement official in the country—was not merely unprofessional, she was unhinged. Called to answer questions about the Department of Justice’s handling of the Epstein files, she instead resorted to name-calling, deflecting, and denying justice for the survivors who sat behind her in the hearing room. (And what on earth was she doing talking about the Dow Jones Industrial Average?).
It was more than an embarrassment (which it most certainly was). It was an indictment of the lawless Trump administration, where we see a pattern of disregard for the Constitution, hostility toward the rule of law, and a willingness to use the powers of government to silence and suppress the rights and freedoms of the people, including the freedom of speech, of the press, of assembly.
Trump and Bondi’s Justice Department attempted to indict six Democratic members of Congress this week. Their “crime”? Reminding members of the military of their oath to protect and defend the Constitution of the United States and their obligation not to follow illegal orders. The DOJ prosecution effort failed, but it revealed a dangerous willingness to weaponize law enforcement against political opponents. As with so much these days, it’s so far beyond the pale and not at all surprising at the same time.
The freedoms our founders enshrined in the Constitution—and that generations of Americans have fought to protect—are under attack from this administration that believes it will not be held accountable. But we can prove them wrong. In our democracy, the people have the final say.
We have our say at the ballot box, which is the work of this team. And we can all commit to vote, and to getting others to vote in 2026. We can also have a say in the places we inhabit, the offices where we work, the groups we belong to. We can have a say in opinion pieces in the paper and letters to the editor. We can have a say on our social media channels. We can have a say by taking this administration to court.
We all need to speak up now. Because, when we do, the voices of Americans will resonate across the country—like the brave Americans in Minnesota, the talented Olympians, the courageous plaintiffs filing lawsuits to stop the lawlessness, and the lawyers arguing them, all saying that this administration is not reflecting who we are and what we value. Their courage is contagious. And, together, everything we do will add up to something, something that is enough to get through these difficult days and to much brighter ones ahead.

* * *
By now, I imagine you've seen at least a few clips of the absolute jackassery from Pam Bondi during yesterday's House Judiciary Committee hearing. It was one of the saddest displays I can remember in modern American politics--someone treating an issue this serious with such carelessness and open contempt for Congress.
And let's be clear about why she acted the way she did. Pam Bondi had an audience of one. She was performing for Donald Trump. That's it. It's the same performance you see every day from MAGA influencers and politicians twisting themselves into knots, trying to invent excuses for why Donald Trump somehow isn't responsible for what's happening with the Epstein cover-up right now.
And let's be clear about something else, too: The reason Pam Bondi feels so comfortable acting this way is because she believes she's untouchable. She believes she'll get a pardon from Donald Trump on the way out the door if it ever comes to that. It's the same reason Kash Patel had no problem lying to Congress in December about whether there was evidence of human trafficking connected to Jeffrey Epstein. It's the same reason so many people in Trump's orbit feel completely at ease committing crimes and lying to the American people. They think there's a get-out-of-jail-free card waiting for them.
But if you look closely, you can see the fractures spreading across the Republican Party. They're there. People are breaking off left and right. Maybe they're not ready to fully walk away from MAGA yet. Maybe they haven't suddenly grown a spine or discovered a shred of character. But the cracks are visible.
The latest talking point from these hacks--one I ran straight into yesterday on Piers Morgan's show--came by way of Clay Travis. A Fox News sports hack. An online influencer. I don't even know what to call him at this point. Yesterday, he decided to cosplay as a legal expert, pretending he has the kind of expertise to explain the Epstein case to the public. I'm not convinced he could tell you the difference between the penal code and or a Trump bible.
So here's their new line, and I've now seen it parroted all over by proudly stupid MAGA influencers. Almost a direct quote here: if the "so-called Epstein victims" really knew the names of their so-called perpetrators, they should just name them.
It's the same energy I got last week when I went on a Daily Wire show--Bar Fight. "Oh, Mike, tell me what crimes you think were committed in the Epstein files. Tell me who you want prosecuted." As if that's some kind of trap. As if demanding accountability is radical.
They think these gotcha questions absolve their king and his minions--Pam Bondi included--of what is inching closer to one of the biggest, ugliest cover-ups in American history. And that's saying something, because our government has done some shit.
What really drives me nuts is this idea that if they stand across from someone like me--a proud Democrat, yes, but more importantly an empathetic human being who still has a soul and isn't a hack--they can intimidate me with, "Mike, what crimes do you want prosecuted?" Like I'm supposed to shrink into a wallflower.
Fuck that.
I get in their faces and I say: I want people prosecuted for abusing kids. I want people prosecuted for trafficking and recruiting those kids. I want people prosecuted for lying to the American people under oath. It's not complicated. It's not controversial. It's not a hard answer.
When they ask, "Who do you want investigated, Mike?" I say: everyone. Anyone who abused kids. Anyone who trafficked kids. Any co-conspirator still unnamed in those Epstein files--based on what we're hearing from members of Congress, Democrat and Republican alike. I want them prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law. I don't care if they're a Democrat or a Republican.
And I don't care because, as much as I joke about being a hack sometimes, I'm not one. I'm a human being having a normal reaction to something horrific. I'm thinking like a parent of a six-year-old who wants to keep my kid safe!

* * *
Asking people to name exactly who should be prosecuted in the Epstein files is a deflection. We don't have access to the full scope of those files, and pretending we do shifts the burden away from the real issue: accountability.
What we do know is that Epstein had a vast network, and Trump's name appears repeatedly in thousands of documents, alongside other political elites and government officials. Anyone in those files who committed crimes should be investigated, prosecuted, and face consequences -- no matter their party or position.
We're talking about taking the word of powerful and wealthy people over survivors, many of whom were children at the time. Trauma affects memory. Fear is real. Testifying is retraumatizing. Some victims may not know the identities of the people who abused them. That doesn't invalidate what happened.
This is a moral issue. Defending or minimizing it isn't about principle -- it's about protecting power. And that should concern anyone with a conscience.
Pam Bondi couldn't even look at the victims yesterday. That's the level of disrespect we're dealing with.
And it's maddening. These people have handed whatever soul they had over to Donald Trump. Everything is for the king. And I honestly don't know if there's a way back for them.
As a practicing Catholic, I believe in forgiveness. I want repentance. I want them to recognize the damage they've done--to this country, to our institutions, to people's mental health, to the economy, to ICE, and especially to the victims who've been caught in the blast radius of this entire Epstein nightmare. People in Trump's inner circle. People like Howard Lutnick. People who keep lying.
And yes, let me be clear: if there are Democrats in those files too, they should be punished to the fullest extent of the law. At bare minimum, anyone who maintained a relationship with Jeffrey Epstein after he became a registered sex offender in 2008 should have to answer for it. No exceptions. No team jerseys.
But these MAGA influencers, these MAGA politicians, the professional hacks like Pam Bond and Clay Travis--they're hollow. That's why Bondi feels emboldened enough to weaponize the personal information and search histories of members of Congress. That's why she thinks screaming clever insults on Fox News for a viral clip will shield her from accountability.
It won't.
Outside of Twitter and conservative media bubbles, this is an 80-20 issue. Most Americans understand what's happening. Most Americans are angry. Maybe not all of that anger will translate into votes--but a lot of it will.
And I believe, come November, it'll be enough for a reckoning.

For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | First Invеstmеnt Updаtеs brоught tо уоu bу Іnception Media, LLC. A 44-year-old illegal immigrant from El Salvador, already charged with raping and murdering 13-year-old soccer player Oscar Hernandez in California last year, **[now faces nine new child sexual abuse counts](https://substack.com/redirect/8ce8997b-5ea4-4ed6-b7ca-689379d29a6d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** involving two other teenage boys.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/beb6cb54-f107-45de-9708-7045ba74c5ae?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **Prior Assault Charges:** Garcia-Aquino faced earlier accusations of sexually assaulting teenage boys in December 2022 and February 2024, both separate cases from the murder.
* **Victim 's Last Contact:** The 13-year-old boy went missing March 28 after traveling by train to visit his coach in Lancaster, California.
* **Murder Details Alleged:** Authorities claim Garcia-Aquino raped Hernandez during the assault that led to his death, then dumped the body roadside in Ventura County.
* **Current Detention Status:** The suspect remains jailed without bail as he awaits trial on the combined murder and expanded sexual abuse charges.

* * *
## Iconic American Girl doll's Ozempic makeover shocks fans
American Girl unveiled its Modern Era Collection on Wednesday, **[reimagining beloved historical dolls like Felicity, Kirsten and Addy in slimmed-down bodies,](https://substack.com/redirect/33d839d7-01c7-4e27-b9f3-4f281b090888?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/33d839d7-01c7-4e27-b9f3-4f281b090888?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)denim jeans and minidresses to mark the brand's 40th anniversary, sparking fury among fans who decry the "Ozempic" transformations as erasing nostalgic charm.

* **Modern Outfits Unveiled:** Classic long skirts swapped for contemporary denim jeans, minidresses and updated hairstyles to appeal to new generations.

name: Eileen for Colorado
subject: Home insurance premiums are skyrocketing in the new year, and Congressional inaction is allowing Coloradans to be priced out of home ownership.
body:
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | [|
---](https://mailchi.mp/8061407d85a6/lauren-boebert-voted-no-on-investing-in-farmers-ranchers-and-rural-communities-15534316?e=1c5f08419c)
|
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Home insurance premiums have been rising nationwide, but Colorado has been hit especially hard. In the past decade,**Colorado has consistently ranked in the top ten for states with the most expensive homeowner’s insurance.** While the national average homeowners insurance increased by around 64% between 2015 and 2024, Colorado experienced a 137% increase in the same period— **more than double the national rate.**
**If we don’t make a change, this issue only stands to worsen as time goes on.** Rural and fast-growing areas are experiencing worsening extreme weather like wildfires and hail storms that increase insurance risks. **Non-renewal rates have impacted rural regions in our district,** making home ownership seem like an impossible goal for younger generations who are facing impossible premiums.
When insurers walk away from Coloradans and leave families without protection, we need representatives who are willing to fight back.**While Lauren Boebert has shown repeated opposition to legislative packages that could have increased disaster relief, Coloradans have been dealing with a housing affordability crisis.**
---
|
---
| | **That’s why Eileen plans to...**
* **🥊 Crack down on price gouging** by standing up to insurance companies who are unfairly increasing prices.
*

* **❤️🩹 Provide tax relief** for working people in order to combat the cost of living crisis that is making homeownership harder to access.

* **🏡 Strengthen rural communities** by supporting home ownership, small businesses, and family-owned farms and ranches.

**Home ownership should not be some far-off dream or unmanageable burden** , it should be the foundation for the small-business owners, farmers, ranchers, seniors, and young people who make our district what it is.****
**Eileen understands how important owning a home is for building a lasting legacy and future** , and she promises to never stop fighting to make this goal achievable for all Coloradans.
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | [**Join Eileen**](https://eileenforcolorado.us12.list-manage.com/track/click?u=400e8fa21dba23169b817268c&id=f0976fd0f0&e=1c5f08419c)** in the fight for fair, equitable, and reliable protections for current and future homeowners.**
---
| |
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | **About our “What’s at Stake” Series** This newsletter focuses on what is on the line for Colorado if Lauren Boebert remains in Congress. Each edition highlights a real issue facing families in our district, what is driving the problem, and how leadership in Washington can make a tangible difference. From rising health care costs to threats to rural hospitals to the economic pressures on working families, the stakes in this election are real.
**We encourage you to share** these newsletters with friends, neighbors, and on social media so our community can have informed, honest conversations about what this election means for the future of Colorado’s Fourth District

subject: URGENT: Trump administration repeals federal pollution limits
body:
To view this mail in a browser, copy https://links.messages.lcv.org/servlet/MailView?ms=MTM0NzcyNzQS1&r=NjA3MDU0MTAzNTc3S0&j=MjQwMDc0MjY5MgS2&mt=1&rt=0 into your browser.
Peter — our January Membership Drive ends tomorrow, and according to our records, we haven’t heard from you yet. Do we have that right? We’re expecting droves of new attacks on the environment from Trump and Congress this year. Already, their Big Ugly Bill ended virtually all money-saving programs for residential clean energy and energy efficiency, they’ve gutted safeguards that keep our air and water clean, and they’ve voted to hand our public lands over to corporate polluters. As we prepare our response, it’s crucial that we hear from ALL of our LCV members. Can you review the information below? Our triple match ends at midnight tomorrow, and we don’t want you to miss out on this opportunity. Until midnight tomorrow, a group of donors will triple the impact of your membership renewal up to $50,0000.Please review your status and renew for just $5 today while our triple match is active >> https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/NvbyBG8_ NAME EMAIL YOUR STATUS N. BLAKE - Current Peter Willis dpwillis67@gmail.com RENEW NOW >> https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/x_ L. GERHARDT - Current It’s critical that we meet our $50,000 fundraising goal for this month. We can’t afford to fall short when Trump has already attempted to: ❌ Halt multiple offshore wind projects that would provide clean affordable power
to millions of people, as well as hundreds of high-paying jobs ❌ Make it easier for companies to pump more toxic and climate pollution into the
air we breathe with little oversight or accountability ❌ Weaken the Clean Water Act by proposing to overturn communities’ rights to
protect their waterways ❌ Open up our public lands to dangerous mining operations and clear the way to
sell off some of the country’s most pristine wilderness to corporate polluters RENEW WHILE EVERY $5=$15 >> https://links.messages.lcv. Our strength is in our collective power at LCV, Peter. When we all move
together, we can hold the line when congressional Republicans and the Trump
administration try to prioritize the needs of corporate polluters and the
ultrawealthy over the needs of everyday people. We’re already starting to see the results — Trump’s approval rating is lower
than ever, and his administration has lost on four court battles in their attempts to stop work on offshore wind projects. If we can keep the pressure on — by mobilizing our supporters and organizing
with our 30 state affiliates across the country to demand affordable clean
energy and keep public lands in public hands — we can win. But we need your help to make that happen, so we’re asking: Will you renew your LCV membership for $5 ahead of tomorrow’s fundraising deadline to help us keep pushing back against the Trump administration’s attempts to put polluters before people? https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/_ Sincerely, Chris, Alex, Kelly, Shae, Liana, Olivia, Sanam, and Alijah
LCV’s Membership Team This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. ---|---|---
Mississippi's alcohol laws are some of the most restrictive in the country, built around a control-state model that assumes government gatekeeping is the only way to manage commerce. For decades, this system has limited consumer choice, insulated entrenched distributors from competition, and treated adults as incapable of making lawful purchasing decisions without state intermediation. House Bill 669 does not dismantle that system--but it meaningfully improves it.
At its core, HB 669 authorizes something Mississippi currently prohibits: the direct sale and shipment of distilled spirits to adult residents. Under existing law, consumers who wish to purchase spirits are effectively forced into a narrow, state-controlled distribution channel. Producers--especially small or specialty distillers--are locked out of reaching Mississippi customers unless they navigate an expensive and highly restricted distributor network. HB 669 opens a new channel for voluntary exchange where none previously existed.
That matters.
Direct-to-consumer shipping expands choice, competition, and access. It allows Mississippians to purchase specialty or limited-run spirits that may never appear on local shelves. It enables small producers to reach customers without surrendering control of their product to a cartelized distribution system. And it treats adults like adults--capable of choosing what to buy and from whom.
Critics argue that HB 669 imposes taxes, permits, and reporting requirements, and that is true. But this critique misses the baseline reality: Mississippi already taxes and regulates alcohol heavily. The bill does not raise general alcohol tax rates or impose new taxes on existing transactions. Instead, it applies Mississippi's existing tax framework to a newly authorized activity. That is not a tax increase--it is the cost of participation in a market that the state previously forbade altogether.
The relevant question is not whether the bill is perfectly free-market. It is not. The real question is whether HB 669 improves liberty compared to the status quo. On that measure, the answer is clearly yes.
Importantly, HB 669 does not mandate participation. No one is required to ship, sell, or purchase spirits directly. The bill simply allows willing buyers and sellers to transact under defined rules. That voluntary expansion of lawful commerce is a net gain for economic freedom, even if it occurs within a regulatory environment that remains too restrictive.
The bill is also notable for what it does not do. It does not expand the state's monopoly over alcohol sales. It does not create a new government-run program. And it does not prohibit existing retailers or distributors from continuing their business. Instead, it introduces competition into a system that has long been closed.
HB 669 is not the end of reform--and it should not be treated as such. Mississippi should continue working toward a simpler, more open alcohol market that reduces protectionism and unnecessary bureaucracy. But progress rarely comes all at once. Sometimes it comes through incremental steps that loosen control and expand choice.
HB 669 is one of those steps. In a state where the default has long been prohibition by regulation, allowing direct-to-consumer spirits shipping is a meaningful improvement--and one worth supporting.

| | Peter, For me, Black History Month isn’t just about looking back at the icons in our history books. It’s about looking around at the history we are making right now. I didn't start fighting for communities of color when I was sworn into Congress. I started on the streets of Milwaukee. From organizing to start a community credit union to protesting for fair housing and voting rights, I’ve been on the front lines my entire life. I learned early on that justice isn't given. It’s won. _The faces of oppression may change, but the fight remains the same._ Decades ago, we were fighting against redlining and overt segregation. Today, we are fighting against voter suppression, economic inequality, and a militarized presence in our neighborhoods that treats people of color as threats. Peter, the best way we can honor the giants on whose shoulders we stand, trailblazers like Vel Phillips, Shirley Chisholm, John Lewis, and Fannie Lou Hamer, is by continuing their work. [**This Black History Month, I am asking you to recommit to that work. Will you sign my pledge to fight for racial justice and equity in 2026?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/125270304/601250303/1621761713?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjQvMS85MzczOSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmYzNkMDMyOS02NzA4LWYxMTEtODMyZS0wMDIyNDgyYTk3MzMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=-BFtR0hv2MIapZQUDojQdDmb9_pdMV0E3xjXnPrrK44=&emci=00f13b24-3408-f111-832e-0022482a9733&emdi=fc3d0329-6708-f111-832e-0022482a9733&ceid=1486204) [TAKE THE PLEDGE »](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/125270305/601250304/1621761713?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjQvMS85MzczOSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmYzNkMDMyOS02NzA4LWYxMTEtODMyZS0wMDIyNDgyYTk3MzMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=-BFtR0hv2MIapZQUDojQdDmb9_pdMV0E3xjXnPrrK44=&emci=00f13b24-3408-f111-832e-0022482a9733&emdi=fc3d0329-6708-f111-832e-0022482a9733&ceid=1486204) Let’s keep making history together. clean_body: Celebrating past victories is not enough - we must continue the work each and every day. | = | | Peter, For me, Black History Month isn’t just about looking back at the icons in our history books. It’s about looking around at the history we are making right now. I didn't start fighting for communities of color when I was sworn into Congress. I started on the streets of Milwaukee. From organizing to start a community credit union to protesting for fair housing and voting rights, I’ve been on the front lines my entire life. I learned early on that justice isn't given. It’s won. The faces of oppression may change, but the fight remains the same. Decades ago, we were fighting against redlining and overt segregation. Today, we are fighting against voter suppression, economic inequality, and a militarized presence in our neighborhoods that treats people of color as threats. Peter, the best way we can honor the giants on whose shoulders we stand, trailblazers like Vel Phillips, Shirley Chisholm, John Lewis, and Fannie Lou Hamer, is by continuing their work. Let’s keep making history together. Look, I know there’s a lot of concerning news right now, and it’s easy to feel disheartened and worried for the future. _But when it comes to taking on Trump, you can bet your bottom dollar that I’m not backing down._ Over the past few weeks, I’ve been meeting with families, seniors, small business owners, and local leaders across NY-16. The message I hear is consistent: people want a government that shows up, listens, and focuses on practical solutions — not chaos, cruelty, or the political horror show we’ve seen unfold across the country. Donald Trump is spending more time ripping funding away from Social Security, stoking fear in immigrant communities, and playing partisan games than focusing on what actually matters: **lowering costs, protecting healthcare, and keeping seniors secure.** I’m interested in making sure NY-16 is heard — and making sure we’re protected from an agenda that’s driven by grievance, revenge, and self-interest. Mark swore an oath to defend the Constitution when he was 22 years old. He’s been under fire in combat and launched into space on a rocket ship for this country. Pete Hegseth and Donald Trump think they can make him sit down and shut up.
#

Team, a federal judge just ruled in favor of Mark’s suit against Pete Hegseth. But before the ink was dry, Pete Hegseth tweeted this:
[](https://act.markkelly.com/go/1389?c0=mek-em-feb26.6dv2ri&refcode=em260212-1-f&t=1&akid=6368%2E6688874%2EByfXRw)
It’s hard to think of anything more un-American than the president attempting to threaten or intimidate people for speaking out against him. But that’s what Trump and Hegseth are doing, and that’s exactly why Mark took him on.
They can’t accept that the Constitution and the law are on Mark’s side. Not after a federal judge ruled against them, not even after a grand jury reportedly rejected an attempt by the Department of Justice to charge Mark with a crime this week.
Mark swore an oath to defend the Constitution when he was 22 years old. He’s been under fire in combat and launched into space on a rocket ship for this country. Pete Hegseth and Donald Trump think they can make him sit down and shut up.

name: Tobias Read
subject: Politico: President Trump says Republicans should take over elections
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260212em-rs [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260212em-rs]
President Trump has crossed a line.
He’s now openly calling for Republicans to take over elections by “nationalizing” them — stripping states of their authority and handing personal control over to a president who already tried to bully, pressure, and lie his way into staying in power.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260212em-rs [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260212em-rs]
That’s not how democracy or our Constitution works. And it’s not going to fly in Oregon — not while I’m Secretary of State.
It’s my job to protect our elections from interference, intimidation, and politicians who believe power belongs to them rather than the people.
We’ve already stopped Trump’s illegal efforts twice in court. We blocked attempts to pry into Oregon’s private voter data. We defended state elections and Oregon’s gold-standard vote-by-mail system. We won, and we’re prepared to do it again.
But make no mistake: these fights are deliberate, ongoing, and relentless. Trump and his allies are counting on states backing down. I won’t — and I know you won’t either.
If you believe Oregon’s elections should be run by Oregonians — not a president who has no respect for our democracy — chip in to support this work today. We need all hands on deck to defend our elections from MAGA Republicans who care more about power than the people. >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260212em-rs]
DONATE NOW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260212em-rs]
If Washington tries to overrule Oregon’s voters, we’ll be ready. If they try to bully our election officials, we’ll defend them. And if they try to take away Oregon’s voting system and hand it to Republicans in Congress, we’ll fight tooth and nail to stop it.
Join me in the fight today, and let’s get to work. >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260212em-rs]
Thank you,
Tobias Read
